actions.question: One action, or several related buttons?

one action.question: What does the action look like?

feedback.question: What are you telling the user?

components.name: BackdropLayer
components.job: A layer that fills its positioned parent with an image, a colour or a scene of your own, from one backdrop value.
useWhen: A page header shows an image or a colour behind its title: pass the layer as the backdrop of ScreenPage, SettingsPage or ContentHeader.
An app stores a backdrop as data, such as a hub that can show an image, a colour or nothing, and draws it in more than one place.
A block of your own needs a covering, contained or tiled image behind its content.

avoidWhen.case: The top of a home screen with art, actions and facts over a backdrop.
A picture that is content, with its own size, alt text and placeholders.

rules: backdrop is one of { kind: "image", src }, { kind: "color", color } or { kind: "node", node }.
An image covers by default; fit contain shows it whole, and fit tile repeats it from the top left at tileSize. position moves it and color fills behind it.
A color or an image color that starts with -- reads as a token, so "--c-tag-violet-dim" paints var(--c-tag-violet-dim).
The layer sits at inset 0 of the nearest positioned parent and takes no pointer events. Set its stacking order with className, as Hero does.
A node fills the layer, and the layer is a size container, so the scene can size itself with container queries.
backdropStyle(backdrop) returns the same background style for an element you draw yourself; a node returns an empty style.
a11y: The layer is hidden from screen readers. A backdrop is decoration; put any picture that carries meaning in an Image with alt text.
Keep the text over a busy image readable with a shade or a scrim, as Hero and ContentHeader do.

path: a picture, a colour or a scene behind a block
tree.rule: BackdropLayer draws an image, a colour or a scene behind a block from one backdrop value.

components.name: Box
components.job: The plain element every block is built from, with an optional sunken or raised surface for a well or a panel.
useWhen: Any element that needs no layout of its own, such as a section, an article, a list or a details block.
A well sunken into the page, such as a list or a text area inside a panel: surface="sunken".
A panel lifted off the page, such as the side panels and the top bar of a studio: surface="raised".

avoidWhen.case: The children line up in a row or a column with a gap.
One self-contained item with a title, a count and actions.

rules: Pick the tag with as; every other prop and a ref pass through to the element.
Without surface it adds no styles of its own.
surface="sunken" sets the sunken fill, a thin border and a medium corner. surface="raised" sets the surface fill, a thin border, a large corner and the first shadow.
A surface paints only the fill, the edge and the corner. Put padding and layout in your own class; any of your rules, such as a smaller corner or a border colour on focus, wins over the surface.
a11y: It adds no role; set as to the element the content needs, such as section or aside for a panel with a heading.
A surface changes only the look, so give a panel its name with a heading or aria-label.

tree.rule: Box is the plain element; surface="sunken" makes it a well and surface="raised" a panel, with the fill, edge and corner from the tokens.

components.name: Callout
components.job: A short note set apart from the text around it, such as a pre-release notice, a banner with a title and an action, or the fine print of a dialog.
useWhen: A note must stay on the page until the cause is gone, such as a pre-release notice or a failed install.
A banner needs a bold first line, a short sentence and one action, such as Get the package.

avoidWhen.case: The message comes and goes on its own.
The note floats over the page and points at one thing.
Something failed to load and can be tried again.

rules: A banner is a Callout with a title: pass title for the bold first line and keep the children to one short sentence.
Pick tone for the meaning: danger for a failure, warning for a risk, info for news, success for a thing that worked.
Pass action for the one button the banner offers, and icon to lead the line; both are optional.
Use variant footnote for fine print under a hairline; it takes no fill and is not for banners.
Put long text or a raw error in details, which sits under the line across the whole box.
a11y: It is a note and adds no alert, so a screen reader reads it in place, title first and then the text.
The title is a plain line, not a heading, so it does not change the outline of the page.
The icon is decoration and is not announced; the tone is never the only carrier of the meaning.

path: a note that stays on the page
tree.rule: Callout is the one note in the flow of the page. A banner is a Callout with a title, and LoadError and ValidationSummary draw on it.

components.name: Center
components.job: Puts its children in the middle on both axes, such as initials in an avatar, an icon in a tile or a message in an empty pane.
useWhen: One item or a short group sits in the middle of a box, such as a waiting message in an empty area.
Initials or an icon sit in the middle of a round or square badge.

avoidWhen.case: The items line up along a column from the top.
The items sit side by side from the start of a row.
Only one axis is centred, or the alignment changes at run time.

rules: Give it a size, through a class or its parent, so there is room to centre in; it fits its content otherwise.
direction defaults to row; set column to stack a title over its message in the middle.
Set inline to sit it in a line of text, sized to its content, such as initials in an avatar.
It is a Flex with align and justify fixed to center and takes every other Flex prop, such as gap, as and className.
a11y: It adds no role; set as to the element the content needs, such as section for an empty pane with a heading.
Centring changes only the look, so the reading order stays the order of the children.

path: items in a row or a column
tree.rule: Center puts its children in the middle of its box on both axes, with the gap and direction of a Flex.

components.name: DensityScope
components.job: Sets how dense the form parts inside it are, once for a whole panel, such as an inspector beside a canvas.
useWhen: A panel holds many small controls in little room, such as the inspector of a layout editor or a tool window.
Every input, Field and Button of the panel should be the small size without passing size to each one.

avoidWhen.case: One control should be small in an otherwise usual form.
A row grid of inputs should be tighter.

rules: Wrap the panel once with density="compact"; every part inside without its own size draws at sm.
A size on a part or on a Field still wins, so a part can stay md inside a compact panel.
Compact also tightens the gaps inside Slider, Checkbox, SegmentedControl, ToggleGroup and DisabledOverlay.
Put a comfortable scope inside a compact one for a section that needs the usual size again.
It draws no box of its own, so put it around the panel without changing the layout.
a11y: It changes sizes and gaps only: names, roles and keys of the parts stay the same.
A compact control is 28 px tall; keep compact for pointer tools, not for touch screens.

path: smaller form parts for a whole panel
tree.rule: DensityScope makes the form parts of one panel compact at once, with the same small size in every app.

components.name: Disclosure
components.job: A line, such as Details or Show log, that shows or hides the content under it when clicked.
useWhen: Some content helps only a few readers, such as the raw text of an error, a log or long release notes.
A list of groups where each one opens on its own, such as the records that point at the one being edited.

avoidWhen.case: The views are peers and only one shows at a time.
The content needs the whole screen or an answer.
A failed load with its raw error.

rules: Write summary as what opens, such as Details, What is new or Show log (24).
Pass defaultOpen to start it open, and onOpenChange to hear each toggle, such as to load a log only once it opens.
A later change to defaultOpen opens or closes it, so a part can open it when a job fails.
Pass open with onOpenChange when the app holds the state, such as Open all over a list of groups; a click then only asks.
Pass end for something at the right of the line, such as a count or a Button; a click inside it never opens or closes the disclosure.
Use size sm for a line in small text, such as inside a settings row.
Pass bodyClassName to lay out the body, such as a column of rows with a gap, in place of a selector on its class.
a11y: It is the browser details element: Enter and Space toggle the line, and screen readers say whether it is open.
Closed content stays in the page, so find in page still reaches it.

path: more content behind a line that shows or hides it
tree.rule: Disclosure shows or hides what is under one line with the browser details element, with one look for every app.

components.name: Gauge
components.job: A small round meter that shows one value against its limit, coloured by the zone the value is in.
useWhen: A load, a temperature or a fill level reads best as a share of its maximum, such as CPU use.
A panel shows a few such readings side by side and each needs its own colour for good, warning and danger.

avoidWhen.case: Progress toward the end of a task, such as a download.
The history of a reading matters more than where it sits now.

rules: Pass min and max when the range is not 0 to 100, and a unit for the value in the middle.
Leave tone out so the zone sets it; set thresholds when the default edges at 60% and 85% do not fit.
Put the danger edge below the warning edge for a reading where low is bad, such as frame rate.
Pick sm for a dense row, md for a panel and lg for a page about that one reading.
a11y: It is a meter: a screen reader hears its label, its value with the unit, and its bounds.
Without a label it is named Meter; give each gauge a label so they can be told apart.

tree.rule: Gauge shows where one reading sits between its bounds, in the tone of its zone.

components.example:
import { Gauge } from '@drizztdourden08/tessera';

const CpuGauge = ({ load }: { load: number }) => <Gauge value={load} unit="%" label="CPU" zones />;

components.name: Grid
components.job: Lays items out in equal columns, such as file tiles, a gallery or the Cards of a dashboard.
useWhen: Items of the same kind sit in equal columns, as many as fit or a fixed count.
A dashboard sets its panels as Cards on as many columns as fit, some two columns wide or the whole row.

avoidWhen.case: The items have their own widths and sit in one row or one column.
Blocks stack in one column.
The user moves and resizes the panels.

rules: Set minColWidth to fit as many columns of at least that width as the box allows; a column never grows wider than the box.
Set columns for a fixed count; when both are set, minColWidth wins.
Set fit with minColWidth when there may be fewer items than columns, such as a lone child: empty tracks collapse and the items share the row.
Wrap an item in Grid.Cell with span={2} to take two columns once two fit, or span="full" for the whole row.
Set dense so a later small item fills the hole a wide one left; the reading order then differs from the order on screen.
Items in a row share its height, and a Card in a Grid.Cell fills the cell.
a11y: It adds no role; pass aria-label, or set it in a section with a heading, when the grid is one region of the page.
With dense, keep the order of the children the order a reader needs, since the keys and screen readers follow it.

tree.rule: Grid lays out equal columns from a count or a minimum width, with Grid.Cell spans and dense packing for dashboards.

components.name: Inline
components.job: A row of children side by side with even space between them, such as an icon and its label, a set of tags or a title with its actions.
useWhen: A few items sit on one line, such as an icon beside its text or a name beside its status.
A title and its actions share a line, with the actions pushed to the far end.

avoidWhen.case: The items run down a column.
The direction changes at run time, or the row needs a setting Inline does not default.
The items line up in equal columns across several rows.

rules: Leave gap at its default of sm for an icon beside its text; pick a larger space token for separate items.
align defaults to center, so an icon lines up with its text; set baseline for words of different sizes.
Set justify to between to push the last item to the far end, and wrap to let a long row flow onto new lines.
It is a Flex fixed to the row direction and takes every other Flex prop, such as as and className.
a11y: It adds no role; set as to ul or nav when the row is a list or a set of links, so screen readers hear the structure.
The visual order is the reading order, so put the items in the order a keyboard user tabs through them.

path: items in a row or a column
tree.rule: Inline lays its children side by side in a row, with a token gap and the items centred across it.

components.name: List
components.job: A bulleted or numbered list of short items, with a nested list drawn one step in.
useWhen: A short run of points, such as the changes in a release or the steps to install.
Text from Markdown is drawn with Tessera parts: Markdown draws every list with List and ListItem.

avoidWhen.case: A list the user adds to, renames and deletes from.
A list of choices to tick.

rules: Put a ListItem inside each List; a nested List goes inside the ListItem it belongs to.
Pass ordered for numbers and start for the first number; without ordered the list has bullets.
Pass bare on a ListItem that holds its own control, such as a Checkbox: it takes the marker off and pulls the control back to the left edge.
Keep each item short; a long item wraps under its marker.
a11y: It is a real list, so a screen reader reads its length and the position of each item.
A nested List is read as a list inside its item.

path: a bulleted or numbered list of short items
tree.rule: List is the bulleted or numbered list; ListItem is one item, and a nested List inside it is drawn one step in.

components.name: PageFrame
components.job: A full-height, padded page that scrolls inside its own frame, for a web app whose html and body stay locked.
useWhen: A web app screen is longer than the window and the frame, not the document, should scroll, such as a settings or account page.
The content should sit in a column of a set width, centred in a wide window.

avoidWhen.case: A website page should scroll with the document, with its own scrollbar and a full-bleed Hero.
Only a box inside a screen scrolls, such as a list or a log.

rules: It is the scroller: the reset keeps html and body locked and the frame is 100dvh tall, so the page behind it never moves.
Set fill to take the height of its parent instead of the window, such as a page inside a pane.
Set width to sm, md or lg to centre the content in a column of that size; leave it out for the full width.
Set padding to md for a 16px page padding in place of the 24px default.
The padding is the page padding token. It is a ScrollArea, so it takes className and the other ScrollArea props except axis, gutter included: set gutter stable when the page reflows with width.
PageFrame keeps the root locked and scrolls inside one frame; PageRoot instead lets the whole document scroll.
a11y: It adds no role, so put a main landmark inside it.
The frame is a scrolling region the keyboard can scroll once it has focus; give it tabIndex 0 when it holds no focusable content.

path: a full-height page that scrolls inside one frame
tree.rule: PageFrame is the page of an app that keeps the root locked; PageRoot is the page of a site that scrolls the document.

components.name: PageRoot
components.job: The root of a website page: it lets the whole document scroll, which a desktop app screen locks, and puts the page inside one box.
useWhen: A website page is longer than the window and the browser should scroll the page itself, with its own scrollbar.
A page has a full-bleed Hero or a sticky header that needs the document to scroll under it.

avoidWhen.case: A desktop app screen scrolls inside its panes and the window stays fixed.
A web app keeps the root locked and scrolls inside one padded frame.
A list or a table scrolls inside a box on the page.

rules: Mount one PageRoot at the top of the page; it sets data-scroll="document" on the html element and restores the old value when it unmounts.
Without a PageRoot the reset still locks html and body, so desktop apps stay exactly as they are.
Open dialogs lock the page again while they are shown, so the page behind does not scroll.
It renders a plain box and takes the props of a div, such as className and children.
PageRoot lets the whole document scroll; PageFrame keeps the root locked and scrolls inside one frame.
a11y: It adds no role, so give the page a main landmark inside it.
The browser scrolls the document, so the keys, the scrollbar and find in page work as on any website.

tree.rule: PageRoot is the one part that turns document scrolling on; everything inside it is built from the usual parts.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.job: A box that scrolls its content, with a styled scrollbar, such as a changelog, a list of cards or a pane body.
useWhen: Content can grow past a fixed height or width, such as a changelog or a grid of cards.
Two boxes must scroll together, through scrollTo and onScroll.

avoidWhen.case: The content always fits and nothing needs to scroll.
The list is long enough that every row must not be drawn at once.

rules: axis picks y, x or both; the other direction is clipped. It defaults to y.
scrollbar slim draws a thin line along the edge that widens under the pointer; native keeps the browser bar.
A slim area reserves its own gutter on the inline end, so opaque children such as cards never cover the line.
Set fade to false when the edges of the content must not melt away.

gutter stable keeps room for a native scrollbar even when nothing overflows. Set it on a page body whose content reflows with width, such as a Grid with fit or minColWidth or a responsive RowGrid, so the scrollbar cannot come and go and flip the layout. It defaults to auto, which takes no room until the content overflows.
Give the box a height, through a class or its parent, or it grows with its content and never scrolls.
a11y: The box is a plain div and keeps the reading order of its children.
Pass tabIndex 0 and a label when the content has nothing focusable, so a keyboard can scroll it.

tree.rule: ScrollArea scrolls content that can outgrow its box and keeps the slim scrollbar clear of the content.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.job: A row of joined buttons that picks one value out of a few, with a highlight that slides to the active one.
useWhen: A short setting has a few choices that all fit on one line, such as a scale or an alignment.
The choices are modes of one view, and the user switches between them often.

avoidWhen.case: The choices are many or have long labels.
Each choice needs a sentence of help.
Several choices can be on at once.

rules: Give each option a value and either a label or an icon.
An icon option takes a hint, and its label reads from it; the icon is a name from the set or any node, such as a pixel icon or a Glyph.
A node passed as icon is drawn as given, so size and colour it yourself; a name is sized by the control.
Pass onDeselect to let a second press on the active option clear the value.
An option takes a tooltip with an optional description and shortcut, placed by tooltipPlacement; its name is the label or hint.
A disabled option takes a string that says why.
a11y: The track is a radio group named by label, with a radio per option and one Tab stop on the chosen one.
The arrow keys, Home and End move and choose; an icon option is named by its title or hint.

tree.rule: SegmentedControl is the joined row that picks one of a few values.

components.name: Select
components.job: A field that opens a list and picks one option, or several, from plain options, from options in labelled groups, or from your own items.
useWhen: The user picks one value from a list too long to show as buttons, such as a country or a sprite size.
The user picks several values from a fixed list and the list does not need typing to find them: pass values and onValuesChange.
The options sit under labelled headings, such as warm and cool colours: pass groups.

avoidWhen.case: The user finds the option by typing, or may type a value that is not in the list.
The list is short enough to show all at once.
The options are actions, not values for a field.

rules: Pass options for a plain list and groups for options under headings. Pass items for objects of your own, with the field that holds the value.
When options and groups are both given, the options come first with no heading, then each group under its label. A group never hides the options.
An option that sits in a group is not repeated in options; put it in one place only.
The app owns the value: pass value and onChange for one choice, values and onValuesChange for several.
Pass grow={false} to keep a fixed width (the token --field-w-inline, 256 px, shrinking to 160 px) beside other tools in a toolbar; TextInput, SearchInput and Combobox take the same prop.
Use NativeSelect instead of Select for a form that posts to the browser, or on a touch screen.
a11y: The trigger is a combobox with a listbox; options are option rows, and a group heading names its block.
The arrow keys, Home and End move through the options, Enter picks, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

tree.rule: Select is the field that opens a list of options, plain or grouped, and picks one or several.

own.name: onChange
own.text: (value: string) => void | (value: ValueOf<T, F> | null) => void

own.name: onActiveChange
own.text: (value: string | null) => void | (value: ValueOf<T, F> | null) => void

components.name: Sparkline
components.job: A small line or area chart of the latest samples, so a reader sees which way a value moves at a glance.
useWhen: A live reading, such as frame rate or download speed, needs its recent history beside the number.
A tile or a row has room for a trend but not for a full chart with axes.

avoidWhen.case: The number and its change matter more than the shape, in a tile of its own.
One value against its limit, with no history.

rules: Pass the samples newest last, and set length to the window, so a new series fills in from the right.
Fix min and max for a reading with known bounds, such as a percentage; leave them out to follow the samples.
Use band for the zone that matters, such as a warning above 80, and dot to mark where the latest sample sits.
Give it a width and height, or a box to fill; it is 32 px tall when nothing sets its height.
a11y: It is hidden from screen readers unless it has a label, since the number beside it usually says the same.
With a label, a screen reader hears the name with the latest, lowest and highest sample.

tree.rule: Sparkline draws the recent samples of one reading as a line or an area, with no axes.

components.name: SpeechBubble
components.job: A box that speaks, with an optional tail toward whoever says it or the part it is about, such as a mascot beside the search palette.
useWhen: A mascot or a guide explains something in a few lines and the tail shows who says it.
A note must float over the page, on its own surface, and point at one thing.

avoidWhen.case: A note that sits in the flow of the page.
A hint for the control under the pointer or focus.
A walk through the screen, one part at a time.

rules: Pass pointer for the side the tail sits on, such as pointer="left" for a bubble to the right of its speaker; it defaults to none.
Move the tail along its edge with pointerOffset, in pixels from the start of that edge; it defaults to the middle.
The tail hangs outside the box, so leave about ten pixels of room on that side.
Leave tone off for a neutral border, or pass a Callout tone to tint the fill and colour the border and the tail.
The fill is opaque, so the bubble reads over any page; pass maxWidth for a narrower bubble than 320 pixels.
Place it yourself, with absolute position or an Anchored part; it sets no position on the page.
Extra attributes and the ref go to the box, so a bubble can be a dialog, a popover or a live status.
a11y: It adds no role. Pass role="status" for a bubble that speaks on its own, or role="dialog" with a label for one that takes focus.
The tail is decoration and is not announced.

path: a note in a bubble with a tail
tree.rule: SpeechBubble is the one bubble with a tail: GuidedTour draws its step card on it, and a mascot speaks through it.

components.name: StackedBar
components.job: One horizontal bar split into the parts of a whole, such as memory by process, with a tooltip and a legend.
useWhen: A total is shared by a few named parts and the reader compares their sizes, such as memory or disk use.
A count of jobs splits by status, each part in its status tone.

avoidWhen.case: One value toward an end, with nothing to split.
Rows of exact figures the reader sorts and filters.

rules: Give each segment a stable id, so a live bar keeps its parts in place from one update to the next.
Set limit to the parts worth naming; the smallest beyond it join one Other part.
Pass total when the parts do not fill the whole, so the room left shows as free track.
Set orientation to vertical for a column beside other columns; give it a height, or a box with a height to fill.
Use status tones when the parts are states and tag colours when they are names; leave color out to cycle the tag colours.
Give a part a description when its name needs a line of meaning; it shows under the name, value and share in its tooltip.
a11y: With a label, the bar is an image named with every part and its value.
The legend lists each part as text, so the values never live only in a tooltip.
A description shows only in the tooltip, so keep it to meaning and never put a value there alone.

tree.rule: StackedBar shows how one total splits into named parts, in a single bar.

components.name: Status
components.job: A read-only word for the state something is in, given as a word and a tone, or as a key of a table of states declared once.
useWhen: A connection, a sync, a session or a draft shows its state beside its name.
A kind of state, such as a session or an engine, shows on more than one screen, so its words and tones live in one table.

avoidWhen.case: The value is a count, or a dot for news.
The value sorts an item into a group the user can filter on.
The state is a step in a task the user walks through.

rules: Pass a word and a tone for a state that shows in one place; pass map and value for a kind of state that shows on several screens.
Declare each table once with defineStatuses, in a constants file beside the model it describes, and import it where the state shows.
Give every word in sentence case; the pill variant sets it in capitals itself.
Set size to sm for a row 18px tall, such as inside a table cell; leave it out for the normal size.
Set dotSize to lg for an 8px dot, and halo for a soft ring in the tone behind it, such as a node that is up; halo draws the dot even without dot.
Set pulse only on states that are still moving, such as starting or syncing.
Pass fallback for a value that can be missing, such as a state not fetched yet.
a11y: The word is the text a screen reader reads; the tone, the dot and the icon add nothing it needs.
Add role status when the state changes while the user watches, so the new word is announced.
An icon from a table is hidden from screen readers and takes the place of the dot.

path: a status, a count or a label
tree.rule: Status draws one word in the tone of its state; with a table from defineStatuses, a state reads the same on every screen.

components.name: Table
components.job: A small static table for facts that are only read: a border, a heavier head, padded cells and optional zebra rows.
useWhen: A few rows of fixed facts, such as the keys of a game and what they do.
Text from Markdown is drawn with Tessera parts: Markdown draws every GitHub table with Table.

avoidWhen.case: Rows the user sorts, filters, selects, groups or resizes.
One label and its value on a line.

rules: Build it from parts: Table holds TableSection parts, a TableSection holds TableRow parts and a TableRow holds TableCell parts.
Pass head on the first TableSection for the header rows; the other TableSection is the body.
Pass header on a TableCell of the head so it is a column heading; pass align left, center or right for the side its text sits on.
Pass striped to shade every second body row.
Pass aria-label to Table to name it. The other table attributes pass through.
A table wider than its box scrolls sideways inside its border; keep the cells to short text.
a11y: It is a real table with a head and a body, so a screen reader reads each cell with its column heading.
Name the table with aria-label when the page has more than one.

path: a small table of facts that is only read
tree.rule: Table draws a static table from TableSection, TableRow and TableCell; DataTable is the table the user sorts and filters.

components.example:
import { Table, TableCell, TableRow, TableSection } from '@drizztdourden08/tessera'; const Keys = () => ( Key Uses W 120
);

components.name: Text
components.job: Interface text in a role, such as a title, a caption or an overline, and the namespace for every text element, such as Text.P or Text.Strong.
useWhen: A label, a caption or a short line of interface copy needs a size and a colour from the scale.
Running text uses the elements under Text, such as Text.P, Text.Strong or Text.Code.

avoidWhen.case: A heading that names a page or a section.
A section title with an action beside it.

rules: Pick the role with variant: title, subtitle, body, label, caption, or overline over a group; with no variant it takes the size and colour of its parent.
Colour it with tone, as on Span: muted for quiet captions, danger for an error.
Use the faint tone for the quietest text, such as a keyboard hint beside a field. It stays at or above 4.5:1 on the main ground, but it is dimmer than muted, so keep it to short secondary hints.
Never colour text with --c-text-disabled; it is under 2:1 and only for text inside a disabled control, borders and decoration.
Set mono for file names, seeds and addresses, and numeric for times and counts that line up.
a11y: It renders a span unless as names another element; pick p, label or a heading element when the text has that role.
Faint text fails the contrast a reader needs, so nothing a user must read or act on may use it.

tree.rule: Text sets interface copy in a role from the scale, and its members draw each text element.

components.name: ToolFrame
components.job: A sunken frame for the thing being worked on, with its toolbar on the top edge, such as an editor, a canvas or a log.
useWhen: An editor or a canvas has tools that belong to it, such as View, Zoom or a filter, on its top edge.
A block of content scrolls inside a fixed frame under its own tools.

avoidWhen.case: A well with no tools of its own.
A raised item with a heading and actions.
A stream of log lines with a filter and Copy.

rules: Pass the tools in toolbar, such as ToolGroups or a FilterBar; it sits on the surface colour over a line.
Give a SearchInput, Select or Combobox in the toolbar grow={false}, so it keeps a set width and sits on one line with the other tools.
The content scrolls under the toolbar; give the frame a height or a flex parent.
Pass padded for space around the content; leave it off when the content has its own, such as a list.
Pass as and aria-label to name it, such as as="section" aria-label="Sprite sheet".
a11y: It adds no role; name it with as and aria-label when it holds the main work of the screen.
The toolbar comes first in reading order, before the content.

path: a frame with a toolbar on its top edge
tree.rule: ToolFrame is the one frame with tools on its top edge: StudioLayout holds its editor in it and LogPanel its lines.

components.name: ToolGroups
components.job: Tools in groups, each under a small label, with a line between groups, for the top bar of a studio or the toolbar of an editor.
useWhen: A bar holds several kinds of actions that read better under a name, such as Save to this app and Export a file.
The toolbar of an editor mixes buttons, toggles and a segmented control, grouped by what they change.

avoidWhen.case: Buttons joined into one control with shared borders.
Actions on one item that fold into More when the room runs out.
A plain row of buttons with no names over them.

rules: Pass groups as { id, label, content }; content holds any controls, such as buttons or a SegmentedControl.
Keep labels short and in sentence case; they name what the tools do, such as View or Export a file.
Pass label to name the whole set when it is not the only toolbar on the screen.
The groups wrap to a new line when the room runs out, so keep each group small.
Pass compact for one row of small controls with the names hidden, such as the toolbar of a studio editor: every control without its own size draws at sm.
Give a SearchInput, Select or Combobox in a group grow={false}: it fills the line otherwise.
a11y: Each group is a group named by its visible label, so a screen reader reads the label before the tools.
With label, the whole set is a group named by it.
With compact, each group keeps its name as aria-label; give every icon button a label, since no name shows above it.

path: tools in groups, each under a small label
tree.rule: ToolGroups names each group of tools with a small label and draws a line between groups; StudioLayout uses it for its bar and its toolbar.

components.name: ActionBar
components.job: The actions on one item in a single row: the primary action last, the ones that do not fit folded into a More menu.
useWhen: An editor header or a list row offers three or more actions on the same item, such as Duplicate, Export and Delete.
The row must stay on one line in a narrow window, with the least used actions one click away under More.

avoidWhen.case: The row holds one icon action that asks before it acts.
The buttons are separate decisions that never fold, such as Cancel and Save in a dialog.
Every action is secondary and none needs to show.

rules: List the actions in the order the user reads them; give the main one kind primary and it sits last, never folded.
Give every destructive action kind danger: it takes the danger look and asks first, in the bar or from the menu.
Pass confirm to name the question and the check, such as Delete Keysanity?; the default asks with the label and a question mark.
Set confirm false on a danger action when the app asks with its own dialog, so the user is not asked twice; true makes any action ask.
Set loading on an action while its work runs: it shows a spinner and cannot be pressed again.
Set nameSuffix in rows that repeat an action, such as the item name, so each button has its own accessible name and tooltip.
Set iconOnly on an action with an icon to draw it as an icon button; its label is the accessible name and the tooltip.
Set keep in a list row, often to one, so every row folds the same way.
a11y: An action with nameSuffix is named by its label and the suffix, such as Delete Friday run, in the button, its tooltip and its question.
The bar is a group named by label, and More is an icon button named More, as tall as the action buttons, that opens a keyboard menu.
An action that asks shows the question with a green check and a quiet cross, focus on the cross; Escape or the cross puts focus back on the action.
The hidden copies used to measure the row are inert and out of the Tab order.

path: actions on one item, folding into More when narrow
tree.rule: ActionBar keeps the actions of one item on one line, styles danger the same way everywhere and asks before it unless the action opts out.

components.name: ActionTile
components.job: A tile with one headline value that also does one thing: runs an action, copies a text, or leads to the full view.
useWhen: A dashboard row sums up a session or a store, and each tile has one obvious next step, such as Stop, Copy address or Clean old runs.
A tile stands for a larger view, such as a widget or a page, and the user should reach it from the tile.
A data domain has its own folder, and the tile should open it beside its main action.

avoidWhen.case: The tile only reads a value, with its trend, its change or a small chart.
A label and its value sit on one row in a list of readings.
The item has several actions of equal weight, such as Edit, Duplicate and Delete.

rules: Give each tile one action at most; put small extras, such as open the folder or copy the path, in tools.
Name the action after what it does to the value, such as Clean old runs or Copy address, not OK or Go.
Use the danger tone for an action that stops or deletes, and primary for the one action the row is about.
Pass onOpen when the tile sums up a view, with openLabel naming that view, such as Show the Players widget.
Write the label in sentence case; it shows as written, at 12 px.
a11y: The tile is a group named by its label, so its buttons are heard with the name of the tile.
Tools and the open chevron are icon buttons named by their label, with the same name as a tooltip.
A copy action or tool confirms with Copied in a polite status region.

path: a headline number that does one thing
tree.rule: ActionTile reads like a StatTile and adds one action, tools and a way to the full view, laid out the same in every app.

components.name: AnchorPicker
components.job: A three by three grid that picks where something is anchored: a corner, an edge or the centre.
useWhen: A canvas or image is resized and the user says which edge or corner stays put.
A tool aligns or places something against one of nine points, such as a watermark or a label.

avoidWhen.case: The user picks one of a few named options in a row.
The user picks one of a short list as radio buttons.
The user picks a position by dragging.

rules: The app owns value; the picker calls onChange with one of top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom or bottom-right.
The default variant dots shows the chosen cell as a filled dot.
The variant arrows shows an arrow in every other cell, pointing away from the chosen one: the look of a canvas resize dialog.
Pass label when the default Anchor does not say what is anchored, such as Keep this edge.
size sm fits a dense panel; md is the default.
a11y: The grid is a radio group with a radio per cell, named Top left to Bottom right, and one Tab stop on the chosen cell.
The arrow keys move in two dimensions and choose; Home and End go to the start and end of the row, and with Control to the first and last cell.

tree.rule: AnchorPicker picks one of nine anchor points, as an image editor does for canvas resize.

components.name: ArmedIconButton
components.job: An icon button pressed twice: the first press arms it and its icon loops a short motion, the second press acts.
useWhen: A row action replaces or removes something, such as loading a save state, saving over one or deleting one.
Several such actions sit side by side on a row and each needs its own second press.

avoidWhen.case: The second press should be a separate check with a cancel beside it.
The action needs a message to explain what it does.
Several actions on one item fold into More when narrow.

rules: Pick the icon by what the action does: load-state to load, save-state to save over, trash-2 to delete.
Name the action and its target in label, such as Load Slot 1: armed, it reads Click again to load Slot 1.
Give load the info tone, overwrite the warning tone and delete the danger tone, as in a save row.
Leave the timeout at 4 seconds; pass timeout={false} only where the button must wait until focus leaves.
Run the action in onConfirm only; onCancel runs when the press times out, loses focus or meets Escape.
a11y: Armed, its name and its tooltip change to the armed label, and a polite status region says it once.
Escape, a blur or the timeout disarms it, and focus stays on the button.
Reduced motion shows the armed pose still, without the loop.

tree.rule: ArmedIconButton shares the one ask of ConfirmIconButton: the same timeout, Escape, blur and focus return.

components.name: Carousel
components.job: Shows one slide at a time from a set, with dots and arrows to move between them, and can turn to the next slide by itself.
useWhen: A home page shows a few featured items in one banner, such as the featured packs of a store.
A small card turns through tips, news or pictures of one pack.

avoidWhen.case: Every item should be seen at once.
Each slide has a name the user picks.
A picture or a video is opened large.

rules: Pass slides as id, label and content; content can be any node, such as a Hero, a Card or an Image.
Write label as the name a screen reader hears for the slide, such as the name of the pack.
Pass turnEvery in milliseconds to turn by itself, 8000 or more; leave it out for a set the user turns by hand.
Pass index and onIndexChange when the app keeps the place, or defaultIndex to start on another slide.
Keep slides about the same height: the box takes the tallest, so the page never jumps.
a11y: The box is a region named by label, with the carousel role description; each slide is a group named 2 of 3 and its label.
It stops turning under the pointer, while focus is inside, on a hidden tab, off screen and with reduced motion; the stop button stops it for good.
Slides are a polite live region only while it does not turn, so a screen reader hears a slide when a person moves it.
Hidden slides are inert, so Tab never lands in a slide that is not shown.

path: one slide at a time from a set
tree.rule: Carousel shows one slide at a time with dots and arrows, and can turn by itself.

components.name: CheckList
components.job: The results of a list of checks, such as a connection test or a diagnostics report, each with its state, what was found and an optional fix.
useWhen: A test runs several checks and the user needs to see which passed, which only advise and which failed.
The checks run one after another, so some are still checking or wait on another.

avoidWhen.case: One long job with steps that run in order, with a bar and a log.
One state shown alone, such as the state of a server.
Labels and values read from a record, with no state.

rules: Name each check after what it tests, such as Game port, and write in detail what was found, such as port 38281 is in use.
Keep warn for advice that does not stop the user, and fail for what must be fixed first.
Give a failed check an action when the app can help fix it, such as Pick another port.
Pass summary to say what the result means, such as Home NAS is not ready.
a11y: The list is a section named by label, Checks by default, and each check a list item.
Each icon is named by its state word, and a check in progress is a Spinner named checking.
The counts are a status region, so a screen reader hears them change as checks finish.

path: the results of a list of checks
tree.rule: CheckList gives pass, advice and failure their own icon and colour, so a test result reads the same in every app.

components.name: CollapseToggle
components.job: The round button on the edge of a panel that folds it to a rail and opens it again, with a chevron that points where the panel goes.
useWhen: A part draws its own panel that folds to its edge and needs the one fold button every Tessera panel uses.
A rail of an app sits beside the main view and folds away, such as a list of profiles.

avoidWhen.case: A side panel with a heading folds beside the main view.
A list sits beside the detail of the picked item.
The left side is the navigation of the app.
A block of content shows or hides below its line.

rules: Pass side="start" for a panel on the left and side="end" for one on the right: the chevron points toward that edge to fold and away from it to unfold.
Pass label with the name of the panel, such as profiles: the button reads Hide profiles or Show profiles.
Pass controls with the id of the panel, and collapsed with onToggle from the state that folds it.

In a pane, place it beside the edge line of the panel, level with its heading, with a 4 px gap (--space-xs) between the line and the button; SidePanel, ListDetailLayout and SplitPane do this for you through their edge. Only the navigation panel SideNav keeps it half over its border.
Prefer SidePanel; a panel of your own folds to its rail: the sunken surface, --side-nav-w wide, the title written sideways.
Use it as it is: it draws at 24 px and takes clicks on 28 by 28 px, and the chevron turns on its own.
a11y: It is a button named Hide or Show and the panel name, with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
The name shows as a tooltip; the chevron is hidden from screen readers.
Keep focus on it when the panel folds, as SidePanel, ListDetailLayout and SideNav do.

path: the button that folds a panel to its edge
tree.rule: CollapseToggle is the one fold button of every Tessera panel: SideNav, SidePanel, StudioLayout and ListDetailLayout all draw it.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.job: A colour picker panel placed in the page, with a field, a hex box, an alpha slider and swatch groups.
useWhen: The user sets a colour and the picker has room in the page, such as a panel in a settings screen.
The user chooses from your own swatch groups, such as a palette: pass swatchGroups.

avoidWhen.case: The picker should open from a swatch button and close again.
The colour is shown, not edited.

rules: Import ColorPicker from @drizztdourden08/tessera/color-picker and ColorPickerPopover from @drizztdourden08/tessera/color-picker-popover. They are not on the main export, so an app that never uses them never loads the colour library.
The app owns the colour: pass value as a hex string and onChange; add alpha and onAlphaChange for an alpha channel, or disableAlpha to hide it.
Pass original to show the colour the user started from, and onReset to put it back.
a11y: The field, the sliders and the hex box are labelled and reachable by keyboard; swatches are buttons with the colour as their name.

tree.rule: ColorPicker is the colour panel placed in the page; import it from the color-picker subpath.

components.name: CommandInput
components.job: A command line on a free text Combobox: Enter sends the command, Up and Down walk the past commands, Tab completes a known one and Escape clears the line.
useWhen: The user types commands for a server, a game or a debug tool.
The user often sends the same command again and should find it with the arrow keys.

avoidWhen.case: The text is a value to keep, such as a name or a note.
The text filters a list as the user types.
The user picks one command from a list of every command.
The text must be one of the listed values.

rules: Pass history when the app already keeps the sent commands; otherwise let the input keep its own and pass storageKey to keep it across launches.
Pass commands, as names or with a description, so typing lists the closest ones under the input; Tab or Right completes the active row or the top one.
Return false from onSubmit when the command was not sent, so the text stays in the line.
Put the replies above the input, such as in a LogPanel, and keep quick commands in actions.
Disable it while there is nothing to send to, and say why in the text near it.
a11y: The input is a combobox named Command, or label, and the key hints under it describe it.
Escape on an empty line passes on, so it still closes a dialog or a popup.
Up and Down move through the suggestions while their list is open, and walk the history once it is closed or the line is empty.
The list is a listbox named Commands and the active row its active descendant; no row is active until the arrows or the pointer reach one.

tree.rule: CommandInput gives every command line the same keys: Enter to send, Up and Down for history and Escape to clear.

components.name: ContentHeader
components.job: The big header of a content container: an icon and a title over a fading backdrop, with a strip of controls after the title and actions at the end.
useWhen: A card, a panel or a page needs a header that names it, with an icon and a title.
Section pills or a status sit right after the title, and a few buttons at the end.

avoidWhen.case: A small heading row inside a panel, with a subtitle and one action.
The title bar of a window, dialog or drawer, with a close button.
A whole page with a header over a body that scrolls.

rules: Leave backdrop out for the default art, pass a scene of your own, or pass null for a plain header. For an image or a colour, pass a BackdropLayer.
Use strip for a few controls after the title, such as HeaderAnchorNav pills, and actions for the end.
Set variant to plain for a title row with no panel: no backdrop, no gradient and no bottom border.
Set compact once the content under it scrolls; it shrinks to a slim row.

On a sub-page, pass back: label names the parent page and onSelect returns to it. It reads Back to and the label, or Back alone with no label, before the icon, and folds to an arrow when the row has no room for it.
level sets the heading tag, h2 by default; pick the level that fits the page outline.
a11y: The title is a real heading; pass titleId to name the container with aria-labelledby.
With live, a screen reader reads each new title, as a status does.
The icon is hidden from screen readers; the title carries the name.
The back button sits outside the heading, so the title stays the name of the page. Folded, the arrow keeps Back to and the page name as its label and shows them as a tooltip.

path: a header with an icon and a title over a block
tree.rule: ContentHeader is the header with an icon, a title and a backdrop that any container can carry.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.job: A menu that opens where the user right-clicks, long presses or presses the menu key, built from the same data as DropdownMenu.
useWhen: A row, a card, a canvas or a tab has actions that belong to it, such as Rename, Duplicate and Delete, and no room for a button each.
The actions are a shortcut to what a menu button already offers, so a power user reaches them where the pointer is.
An app opens the menu itself, for example from a gesture on a canvas, and passes the point.

avoidWhen.case: The menu hangs from its own button.
The actions must be visible without a gesture.
The user looks for any action in the app by name.

rules: Wrap the target in ContextMenu and pass groups; the menu opens at the pointer on right-click and on a long press with touch.
Never make the context menu the only way to an action; repeat each action in a button or a menu button.
Shift+F10 and the menu key open the menu under the focused element, so the target must hold or contain something focusable.
Items, groups, kinds and sub-menus are those of DropdownMenu; the menu flips to stay in the window.
To drive it yourself, pass open, point and onClose; add onOpen to learn where a gesture asked for the menu.
Set disabled to leave the browser menu in place, and longPress off when a long press already means something on the target.
a11y: The menu is role menu, with the keyboard of DropdownMenu: arrows, Home, End, typing and Escape.
Opened with the keyboard, the menu takes focus on its first item and returns it to the element that opened it on close.

Focus returns the same way when you drive the menu with open: after Escape, a pick or open set to false it goes back to the opener, and it stays put when the user clicked into another focusable element.

path: a menu at the pointer, opened by right-click or long press
tree.rule: ContextMenu opens a DropdownMenu at the pointer, or under the focused element from the keyboard.

components.name: ControllerSilhouette
components.job: The outline of a controller, one stroked line with no fill, for the app to draw its own glyphs, labels and lines on.
useWhen: A bindings screen points from each control of a pad to the action it does, with its own glyphs and leader lines.
A tutorial or a help card shows a pad and marks the few controls it talks about.

avoidWhen.case: One button or stick glyph inline, such as a prompt in a sentence.
A keyboard with keys marked or held.

rules: A live layout that lights every input of a pad from its state belongs to the app to build: draw it on CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_PATHS, place its marks from anchor data from the app or from Brock (brock-input exports CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_ANCHORS) inside CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_VIEW_BOX, and use InputIcon for the glyphs.
Pick the variant from the pad family: offset for Xbox shapes, symmetric for PlayStation shapes, nintendo for Switch Pro shapes and pad for a pad with no sticks or triggers.
Draw on it with children made of the Svg primitives. They sit inside the SVG on top of the outline, in viewBox units.
The viewBox is CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_VIEW_BOX, 0 0 400 260, for every variant. It never changes, so coordinates stay valid.
To draw the outline in your own SVG, take its path d from CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_PATHS[variant], in the same viewBox.

Marks are placed from the anchor data of an app or of Brock, never from Tessera, which ships no anchors. The package @drizztdourden08/brock-input exports CONTROLLER_SILHOUETTE_ANCHORS and the anchor ids. Nothing is drawn at an anchor, it only says where a control sits on the real pad, in viewBox units.

Sources. offset, symmetric and nintendo are drawn by hand with reference to Noun Project icons: XBOX Controller (icon 5652517) by Daniel Finnegan, pro controller (icon 5602909) by Eliran Bensadoun and playstation controller (icon 1751312) by dinnerchief. No path data is taken from them. pad is traced from SNES-Controller-Flat.jpg by Evan-Amos, Wikimedia Commons, public domain. Each outline is one mirrored half of smooth curves, with no brand marks.
a11y: The figure is named by label, Controller by default.
The SVG is hidden from screen readers, children included. Give what the marks say in text outside it too, such as a list of bindings.

path: a blank controller to draw on
tree.rule: ControllerSilhouette draws only the outline of a pad, so each app places its own marks from its own anchor data.

components.name: ControlMenu
components.job: A dropdown of settings behind one button: each row is a label with one compact control, and the panel joins its button like a DropdownMenu.
useWhen: A tool, a panel or a widget has several settings that are not worth a page of their own, such as the options behind a gear.
The settings take richer controls than a menu item: a SegmentedControl, a Slider, a Select or a NumberInput with its buttons on the sides.
Some settings belong together and can wait one step further, in a sub-panel beside the panel.

avoidWhen.case: Every entry is an action, an on or off check, or one choice from a short list.
The settings are many, need explanations, or are saved with the profile.
The settings should stay on screen while the user works.

rules: One ControlMenuRow holds one control at size sm, with a short label; long explanations go in hint or about.
Every control applies at once; a ControlMenu has no Save or Cancel.
Group related rows with ControlMenuGroup, and move rows used less often into a ControlMenuSub.
Turn filter on when the panel holds more than about eight rows; it narrows rows by label, and rows of a sub-panel show inline under its name.
Name the panel with label when the trigger is an icon, such as "Players options".
size sets the trigger: sm by default, md beside 39 px fields, xs in a dense bar such as a widget title bar.
panelData sets data attributes on the panel and on every sub-panel, so code outside can tell this menu from other ControlMenus; it changes nothing on screen.
a11y: The trigger is a button with aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; the panel is a dialog named by label.
Opening moves focus to the filter, or to the first control. Tab moves through the controls, and the arrow down key leaves the filter for the first control.
Right arrow, Enter or Space on a sub-panel row opens it and focuses its first control; Escape closes the innermost panel first and gives focus back.
Each row hint is read into the hint line at the bottom, and about adds an info tooltip described to screen readers.

tree.rule: ControlMenu keeps several small settings one click away without a page or a dialog.

components.example:
import { ControlMenu, ControlMenuRow, ControlMenuSub, SegmentedControl, Slider, Toggle } from '@drizztdourden08/tessera';

const DENSITY = [{ value: 'cozy', label: 'Cozy' }, { value: 'compact', label: 'Compact' }];

const ViewOptions = (props: { density: string; zoom: number; sounds: boolean; onChange: (patch: object) => void }) => (
  <ControlMenu trigger={{ label: 'View options', icon: 'sliders-horizontal' }} filter>
    <ControlMenuRow label="Density" hint={{ label: 'Density', description: 'How much room each row takes' }}>
      <SegmentedControl size="sm" aria-label="Density" value={props.density} options={DENSITY} onChange={(density) => props.onChange({ density })} />
    </ControlMenuRow>
    <ControlMenuRow label="Zoom">
      <Slider size="sm" value={props.zoom} min={50} max={200} onChange={(zoom) => props.onChange({ zoom })} />
    </ControlMenuRow>
    <ControlMenuSub label="Sounds" icon="volume-2">
      <ControlMenuRow label="Play sounds">
        <Toggle size="sm" checked={props.sounds} onChange={(sounds) => props.onChange({ sounds })} aria-label="Play sounds" />
      </ControlMenuRow>
    </ControlMenuSub>
  </ControlMenu>
);

components.name: CopyButton
components.job: A button that copies a text to the clipboard and confirms it with a check and the word Copied.
useWhen: One action copies something the user does not see in full, such as debug info or a whole log.
A panel needs a copy action beside its other buttons, with or without its word.

avoidWhen.case: The value itself is on screen and the copy belongs at its end.
Labelled values sit together in a panel, some of them to copy.

rules: Name the button after what it copies, such as Copy address or Copy debug info.
Pass a function as text when the text is costly to build or changes often, so it is built at the click.
Keep it icon only in tight rows and toolbars; show the word where the button stands alone.
Use size xs only in a dense row such as a tile tool strip: it draws a 12 px icon with a 24 px hit area.
a11y: An icon only button is named by its label and shows the same name as a tooltip.
After a copy, a polite status region says Copied once, and the name reads Copied for two seconds.

tree.rule: CopyButton writes to the clipboard through the one copy path every Tessera part uses, with the same check and announcement.

components.name: CopyValue
components.job: A value the user often copies, such as an address, a seed or a key, shown with a copy button at its end.
useWhen: A room address, a seed, a fingerprint or an ID sits in a status bar, a card or a dialog.
A long value has to fit one line and still be copied whole.

avoidWhen.case: Labelled values sit together in a panel, some of them to copy.
The text to copy is not on screen, such as debug info.

rules: Pass label as a short lower case name, such as room address, so the button reads Copy room address.
Set mono for codes, keys, addresses and numbers the user may read back character by character.
Use truncate middle for keys and fingerprints, where the last characters tell two values apart.
Pass text when the string to copy differs from what is shown, such as a full link behind a short name.
To copy the value of a StatRow, pass a CopyValue as its value; it takes the size of the row.
a11y: The value and its button form a group named by label.
A cut value is read whole by a screen reader and shown whole on hover.
The button says Copied through a polite status region after a copy.

path: a status, a count or a label
a value to copy, such as an address or a key
tree.rule: CopyValue keeps the value selectable and puts the copy button at its end, with the same check and announcement as every copy.

components.name: DataTable
components.job: Records as rows and columns the user sorts, groups and picks from, such as the players of a session, with the columns taken from a schema.
useWhen: The user browses many records and sorts, groups, reorders or resizes the columns.
A group can hold hundreds of rows, such as every peer the app has seen, and the table must stay fast.

avoidWhen.case: A short list the user edits in place, one input per column.
A few rich rows with their own actions and no columns to sort.
Files with their size, date and open buttons.

rules: Give it rows, a schema and getRowId; the columns come from the schema, and viewKey keeps the layout between visits.
Pass fallbackGroupBy to open grouped, and defaultExpanded, a list of group keys or a function of the key and its field, to choose the groups that start open; leave it out to open them all.
Set footer to false to leave out the bar at the bottom: the sort and group line, the row count and the options menu with its add column, clear sort, clear group, fit and reset actions.
Set a unit on a number field, or units in the schema config, to write 12.4 MB in the cell; sort, group and filter still read the number.
Keep the rows in the app and pass them whole; from virtualizeFrom rows, 200 by default, the table draws only the rows in view.
Set virtualizeFrom lower for rows that are costly to draw, or to Infinity to draw every row.
Pass selectable with selectedIds and onSelectionChange to pick many rows; the app keeps the selection.

Pass groupActions(groupKey, rows) to draw icon buttons at the end of a group header, as the same action list as an ItemCard; rows holds every row of the group, collapsed or not, so select all in this folder needs no lookup.

Pass onRowMove(fromKey, target) to add a grip cell; the user drags the grip or presses Up or Down on it. target is index, the new place among the rows shown, beforeKey and afterKey, the rows the drop lands before and after, and groupKey, the group it lands in, none when ungrouped; use the keys and groupKey for grouped data, since a shown index does not map to it. A drop in another group arrives even when the order of the rows is unchanged.
Pass rowDragData(row) to make rows draggable to a drop target of the app; each entry of the record is written to the dataTransfer by type, and the app decides what a drop means.
Pass renderCell(row, path) to draw a cell yourself, such as a thumbnail beside a name; return undefined to keep the schema rendering of that cell.
A button, link, input, tooltip trigger or any element marked data-cell-control inside a cell does not select the row or run its handlers; a plain cell still does.
Pass rowHeight, the name of a size token such as size-64, for rows taller than the default; it also sets the height of drawn rows when the table is long.

Pass rowState(row) to mark a row active, pending, error, warning, muted or fresh; the row shows it as an edge, a tint or a lower contrast, warning being a needs-a-look bar and fresh a soft info tint for rows that just arrived, and a selected row keeps the selection background.
Set headerCase to upper for capital column labels with wide letter spacing; the labels you pass keep their case in the data.
Pass sort with onSortChange to own the sort, and expanded, a set of group ids, with onExpandedChange to own the open groups; without them the table keeps both.
A group id comes from groupUid(parentId, path, key), with an empty parent id for a top group; defaultExpanded does not apply while expanded is given.

Pass detailRowId with renderDetail(row) to open a panel under one row, such as an inline confirm or a small form; it spans every column, works in groups and with sort, and the app keeps the id and clears it from onDetailClose.

Give ref and call getRects() for a rect of every row from the layout, drawn or not, with the rows of collapsed groups left out, for useMarqueeSelect({ getRects }); pass scrollRef, bind and overlay as on VirtualGrid.
a11y: The table is a grid of rows and cells; a selectable table is multiselectable and each row carries aria-selected.
Ctrl and Shift click extend the selection and Escape clears it, from the grid or from a checkbox.
A group header is a button that says whether the group is expanded.
A group action is a button named by its label, after the group button in the tab order, and a click on it does not toggle the group.
The grip of a row is a button; Up and Down move the row by one place, focus stays on the grip, and a polite live region says where the row went.
The detail is a row with one cell that spans the columns, placed after its row in the tab order; Escape inside it calls onDetailClose unless a field already used the key.
A checkbox in a row that scrolls out of view stays drawn while it has focus, so the keys keep working.

path: rows and columns to sort and filter
tree.rule: DataTable gives every collection the same columns, menus and grouping, and draws only the rows in view when the collection is long.

own.name: groupActions
own.text: (groupKey: string, rows: readonly T[]) => readonly ActionItem[]

components.name: DateText
components.job: A date or a time in any common format, such as 5 minutes ago, Today, 21:40 or 16 October 2026, with the full date on hover.
useWhen: A list row, a card or a panel says when something happened, such as when a save was made.
A date has to follow the app's language and stay correct as time passes, such as 5 minutes ago.

avoidWhen.case: The date is already text the app wrote itself.
Labelled values sit together in a panel, a date among them.

rules: Pass the raw moment as value, a Date, an ISO string or epoch ms, never text the app formatted.
Use relative for how long ago, calendar for a list of recent saves, date or datetime for records.
Use elapsed for a running job, such as running 4m 03s; set label to the word before it, already translated.
Set length short on elapsed for one unit, rounded down, such as 5s, 12m, 3h or 2d; it ticks by the unit shown.
Leave length unset first: each format starts at the length that reads best.
Set the locale and the words Just now, Today, Yesterday and Tomorrow once, in the dates strings.
For a table column, set SchemaConfig.dates; for text outside React, call formatDate with the same format.
Set the unit letters of elapsed and the order of label and time in the dates strings.
Turn tooltip on for a short format whose exact moment matters, such as time or weekday.
a11y: The text is a time element whose datetime attribute holds the exact moment.
Set focusable when the full date is the only way to read the exact moment, so the keyboard reaches its Tooltip.
A ticking elapsed value is not a live region, so a screen reader is not read every second; the Tooltip holds the exact start.
Figures are tabular, so a time that redraws keeps its width and its neighbours stay put.

path: a status, a count or a label
a date or a time, such as 5 minutes ago
tree.rule: DateText formats a moment with the browser's Intl, in the app's locale, and keeps relative, calendar and elapsed text up to date from shared timers, paused while the page is hidden.

components.example:
import { DateText } from '@drizztdourden08/tessera';

const SaveTime = ({ savedAt }: { savedAt: number }) => <DateText value={savedAt} format="relative" />;

components.name: Dialog
components.job: A modal that asks one question, with a message, a confirm button and a cancel button, and room for a short body.
useWhen: The user must confirm an action, acknowledge a notice or answer a short question before going on.
A short form or a block of text, such as a README or a list of details, sits under the message.

avoidWhen.case: The dialog has its own layout, its own buttons or no question to answer.
A long job runs and the user may hide it or cancel it.

rules: Pick the size from the content: sm for a question, md for a form, lg for a README or a table; the default is sm.
The width follows the content between the min and the max of the size, and never passes the window minus a margin.
The height grows with the content up to the window minus a margin; the header and the buttons stay and only the body scrolls.
Set steady when the width must not move while the content changes, such as an error that appears under a form.
Use variant danger for an action that cannot be undone; focus then starts on cancel.
a11y: The dialog is modal and named by its title; Tab stays inside it and Escape cancels.
Focus starts on confirm, or on cancel for danger, and returns to the opener on close.
A body that scrolls keeps the header and the buttons in view.

path: a question the user must answer
tree.rule: Dialog holds a message and a confirm and a cancel button, and takes its width from its content within the size.

components.name: DialogShell
components.job: The frame of a modal: a backdrop, a panel with a header and a close button, a scrolling body and a row of actions.
useWhen: The dialog has its own body and its own buttons, such as a details view, a form or a README.
A composite needs a modal frame with focus, Escape and the backdrop handled for it.

avoidWhen.case: The dialog asks one question with confirm and cancel.
A long job runs and the user may hide it or cancel it.

rules: Pass size sm, md or lg; each has a min and a max width from tokens, and the default is sm.
The width follows the content between the min and the max, and never passes the window minus a margin.
The height grows with the content up to the window minus a margin; the header and the actions stay and only the body scrolls.
Set steady to pin the width to the max of the size, for a body whose content changes, such as a wizard step or an error line.
Set dismissable to false while a save runs, so only your own actions close it.
a11y: The panel has role dialog and aria-modal, and the title names it.
Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside; Escape and the close button close it unless it is not dismissable.
Focus moves in on open and returns to the opener on close.

path: a dialog with its own layout
tree.rule: DialogShell gives the frame, the focus and the scrolling body, and leaves the content and the buttons to you.

components.name: DocumentTabs
components.job: The strip of open documents above an editor: a tab per document with an unsaved mark and a close button, put in order by drag or keys, scrolling when they do not fit.
useWhen: The user has several documents open at once and switches between them, such as the drawings in a pixel art editor.
The user closes a document from its tab, and the app may need to ask first because of unsaved changes.
The user puts the open documents in the order they like.

avoidWhen.case: The tabs are fixed views of one area, with no close and no reorder.
The tabs split one long form into groups with counts.
The items are a short list of rows the user edits and puts in order.

rules: Keep the tabs and the active id in the app; the strip only draws them and calls onActivate, onClose and onMove.
onClose only asks to close. The app may refuse, for example to confirm unsaved changes first; the tab stays until the app removes it from tabs.
onMove gets the old and the new index; change the order of tabs there.
Set unsaved on a tab to show a dot that stays beside the close button on hover and focus.

Set status on a tab to show where it is, as a small dot before the title: a tone (info, success, warning, danger and the rest of the Status tones), a label and an optional pulse. It is not the unsaved mark; a tab can have both.
title is the text on the tab, cut with an ellipsis; tooltip is the hover text and defaults to the title.
When the tabs do not fit, the strip scrolls and keeps the active tab in view. Pass overflowMenu to add a menu that lists every tab.
Show the document of the active tab beside the strip; DocumentTabs draws no panel.

Pass onTabContextMenu to open the app menu of a tab. It gets the tab id and the event, from a right click, the Menu key or Shift+F10 on a focused tab. Call preventDefault on a mouse event to hide the browser menu.
Pass look="raised" for tabs with a surface fill and a lifted selected tab. Any look takes the fills from --document-tab-bg and --document-tab-bg-selected, which default to no fill.
Pass onAdd to draw a + icon button after the last tab, inside the strip. Its label is translated from the strings, and onAdd only asks: the app adds the document to tabs.
a11y: The strip is a tablist named by label, and each tab is a button with role tab and aria-selected set on the active one. Only one tab is a tab stop.
Left and Right move focus from tab to tab and wrap, Home and End go to the first and the last. Enter or Space activates the focused tab.
Delete or Ctrl and W asks to close the focused tab. The close button of each tab is named Close and the title, and is not a tab stop.
Alt and Left or Right moves the focused tab. Focus stays on the tab, and the move is announced.
A tab with unsaved changes says so to screen readers, and so does the label of its status. The dot is never the only signal: pick a label that names the phase. Middle click closes a tab.
The Menu key and Shift+F10 on a focused tab call onTabContextMenu with the tab id. The add button is a named button and a tab stop of its own.
The drop line follows the pointer while a tab is dragged, and the strip adds no motion when the user asks for less.

path: between the open documents of an editor
tree.rule: DocumentTabs is the strip of open documents the user switches, closes and reorders, the same way in every editor.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.job: A menu of actions, checks, choices and sub-menus, built from data, that hangs from its own button or from an anchor.
useWhen: A view has more actions than its toolbar can show, or actions used too rarely to earn a button, such as Export or Reset layout.
A few on or off checks or one choice from a short list sit with those actions, such as which panels show.
An action undoes work and the menu is where the user finds it: kind confirm asks with a second press, without a dialog.

avoidWhen.case: The entries are settings with richer controls, such as a slider or a number.
The user picks one value for a form field.
The actions belong to one item and should show while there is room.
The user looks for any action in the app by name.

rules: The app owns every checked value and every action; the menu only calls onSelect and draws what it is given.
A check or radio item that is off shows a faint centred dot; turned on, the dot morphs into a check or a filled radio in the menu tone, so an off item never shows a mark.
Give an action that undoes work kind confirm: the first press reads Click again to and the label, in the danger tone; the second runs it.
Give an action that deletes, such as Delete in a row menu, tone danger, so it reads in the danger tone at rest; a confirm item turns red only while it asks.
Pass confirm on such an item for words of your own; the item returns to its label on Escape, on leaving it or after four seconds.
An item icon is a name from the set, iconify data such as an imported Lucide icon, Icon path data, or any element.
Split groups by meaning with a label or a separator; turn on filter past about a dozen items.
Give an item onHighlight to start loading what it opens: it runs once each time the item is hovered, focused or reached with the arrow keys, and never while it is disabled.

Give an item data to put data attributes on it, such as { "data-menu-entry": "rename" }, and ariaDescription for a hint a screen reader adds after the label; description is already read as part of the item.
The trigger keeps its icon while the menu is open; to show another, change trigger icon from onOpenChange.
size sets the trigger: sm by default, md beside 39 px fields, xs in a dense bar such as a widget title bar.

align sets the edge of the trigger the menu lines up with: auto by default, so a trigger in the right half of the window gets its menu under its end, opening to the left at its full width; pass start or end only when the layout needs that one edge.
Anchored menus take side: below or above a button, right or left of a tool in a rail. Right and left line up with the top of the anchor and flip to the other side when there is no room.

openOnHover on a trigger opens the menu after a short delay and closes it a moment after the pointer leaves both; click and the arrow keys still work. An anchored menu takes the same through hover, with focusOnOpen off so a hover does not take focus.

To open a menu from a button of your own on hover, call useHoverOpen({ open, byHover, anchorRef, onOpen, onClose }) and spread the result on the button; pass it as hover to an anchored menu. byHover is true when the hover opened it, so a click or key opening stays open.
a11y: The menu is role menu named by label; items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio, and a confirm item stays a menuitem.
The arrow keys, Home, End and typing move through the items; Escape closes the menu, or first returns an asking item to its label.
The label of a confirm item is a polite live region, so the question is read when it shows, and the item keeps its width.

tree.rule: DropdownMenu keeps rare and secondary actions one click away, and asks before the ones that undo work.

components.name: DynamicInput
components.job: One field built from a pattern of typed slots, muted text and icons, such as a time, a price with its currency or a lobby code.
useWhen: Several small values read as one, such as a time, a date, a size, a server address or a phone number with its country.
A text value follows a fixed shape, such as a host name or a lobby code with its own characters.
The field has to check itself, by slot or as a whole, and show its own error.

avoidWhen.case: One plain line of text or a single number is asked.
A number is typed on its own, with a stepper or a unit.

rules: Write the shape in the pattern, such as {hh:hour 12h}:{mm:minute}, and keep the value as one object keyed by slot name.
Put it in a Field for the label, hint and size.
A text slot takes digits, letters or alnum in the pattern. For any other set, pass slots with chars, a string or a Set of the allowed characters.
Pass aliases, from typed to stored, to read a typed character as another, such as I and L as 1. A slot entry wins over the pattern one.
Do not map an alias to a character that is itself an alias, because the text is cleaned again on every key.
chars and aliases follow the case of the slot, so write them in either case.
Pass validate on a slot or on the pattern, from the value to a message or nothing. A message turns the field invalid and shows under it.
An empty slot reaches validate as null. Return nothing for it unless the slot is required.
The invalid prop wins over validate, and a Field with an error shows its own message.
a11y: The field is a group named by the Field label, and each slot is named by its quoted label.
An invalid field sets aria-invalid on its slots and describes them by the message, which is announced as an alert.
Tab and Shift+Tab move between slots, and a choice slot opens with the arrow keys.
