tree.rule: DynamicInput reads a pattern of slots, so a time, an address or a lobby code is one field with its own characters and checks.

components.name: FileList
components.job: The files a job made or an app keeps, one row each with its type icon, name, size and date, and buttons to open it or show it in its folder.
useWhen: A job writes output files the user opens next, such as a generated seed, a spoiler log or a save.
A report or a settings page lists log files or attachments the user may open or find on disk.

avoidWhen.case: Many files to sort, filter or pick from.
Rows that are not files, with their own columns and action.
One path the user reads or copies.

rules: Pass size in bytes and modified in milliseconds; the list writes them, so every app shows them the same way.
Pass onOpen and onReveal when the app can open the file and its folder; leave them out and the buttons go.
Write empty as why there is nothing yet and when files will show, such as once the seed is generated.
Give a file an icon only for a type of the app, such as a save file; common types take theirs from the extension.
a11y: The list is named by label, Files by default, and each file is a list item.
The buttons are named after the file, such as Open server.log and Show server.log in its folder, with a tooltip.
The date is a time element with its full timestamp.

path: files, with their size, date, open and reveal
tree.rule: FileList gives every file the same row, with the size, the date and the two ways to reach it.

components.name: FloatingPrompt
components.job: A bar at the foot of a region that asks a question with actions such as Apply and Cancel, and blocks the region until the user answers.
useWhen: The user must answer before going on in one area, such as applying or dropping a change to a canvas, while the rest of the app stays usable.
A question needs actions that stay on screen until chosen, in the look of a Toast.

avoidWhen.case: The whole app must wait for the answer.
A short message passes by itself and needs no answer.
A note stays on the page and blocks nothing.

rules: Put it in a positioned parent, beside the region it blocks: it covers that parent and its siblings go inert.
Set scope to window only when the whole page must wait; it then covers the window and everything outside the bar goes inert.
Pass actions as data, each with an id, a label and onSelect; the app owns open and closes it from onSelect.
Mark one action cancel for the way out: Escape runs it, and it draws as a ghost button.
Keep the message to one short sentence that says what will happen, such as Apply the 3 pending edits to the canvas.
Use variant for the tone, the same names as Toast; info is the default.
a11y: The bar is an alert dialog that is not modal to the app: a screen reader reads its message at once, and only the region it covers is out of reach.
On open focus moves to the first action, Tab stays in the bar, and on close focus returns to where it was.
The siblings of the bar in its parent are inert while it is open, so the region gets no pointer or keyboard input.
Escape runs the action marked cancel; with none, Escape does nothing.
Pass label when the message is not enough to name the bar; otherwise the message names it.
Under reduced motion the bar and its layer appear with no animation.

path: a question that blocks one region until it is answered
tree.rule: FloatingPrompt asks the user to answer before going on in one region, with actions from data and the look of a Toast.

components.name: FormGroupTabs
components.job: The top of a long form split into groups: a search over the options, Show advanced, and a tab per group with how many options changed.
useWhen: A form has dozens of options in named groups, such as the option groups of a game preset.
The user needs to find an option by name and see which groups hold changes.

avoidWhen.case: The screen is the settings of the app, with a header over a scrolling body.
Only the tabs are needed, with no counts or search.

rules: Give each tab count, the number of options in the group, and changed, how many differ from their default.
Pass onQueryChange and filter the rows of the form with the query; the tabs stay.
Pass onAdvancedChange with advancedCount to show or hide the options tagged advanced.
a11y: The tabs are Tabs, with their arrow keys, and each tab reads its label, its changed count and its badge.
The search box and the switch are named by their own words.

path: a long form split into tabs
tree.rule: FormGroupTabs shows where the changes are in a long form and how to find an option, the same way in every app.

components.name: FormRow
components.job: One option of a long form: its name and help on the left, its control on the right edge, a changed mark and a reset after the name.
useWhen: A form lists many options built from a schema, such as the options of a game preset, each with a default to go back to.
The user needs to see at a glance which options differ from their default.

avoidWhen.case: The row is an app setting with a live hint, compact or read only.
A short form needs a label, a hint and an error around each input.

rules: Set changed when the value differs from its default, and pass onReset to put the default back; the reset sits after the name and is absent while the value is the default.
The control column is end-aligned, so every control of a list of rows shares one right edge.
Write problem as what blocks the save and what to do, such as Not saved: fix the JSON first.
Tag rare options with advanced, and hide them behind Show advanced in FormGroupTabs.
Write the whole description: past descriptionLines lines, 2 by default, it folds behind More and Less, so the app needs no fold of its own.
Pass descriptionOverflow="hint" when rows must keep one fixed height: the description clamps to its lines, there is no More, and an info mark offers the full text in a tip when it is cut.
Pass descriptionOverflow="clip" for a plain clamp with no More and no info mark, when the full text is shown elsewhere.
Pass help for a note only some users need: it sits behind a ? after the name, shown on hover, focus or click, not on the page.
a11y: The control gets the id, label and notes of the row, as inside a Field, so it is named by the option.
A problem is an alert and marks the control invalid; Reset is named Reset and the option.
More and Less is a button with aria-expanded that controls the folded text.
In hint mode the full text stays in the page for screen readers, and the info mark is one Tab stop that opens the same text.
The ? of help is one Tab stop named Help, and the note opens on keyboard focus as its description.

path: one option in a long form, with a reset
tree.rule: FormRow lays out the name, the control, the changed mark and the reset of an option the same way in every app.

components.name: GuidedTour
components.job: A tour of a screen, step by step: one part stays lit with a glow while the rest dims and blurs, a bubble explains it and the mascot presents it.
useWhen: A first run shows a new user around a screen, one part at a time.
A new feature needs a short walk through the parts it touches, such as a panel that opens.

avoidWhen.case: One shortcut is taught on a drawn keyboard.
A hint explains one control on hover or focus.
A task is done in steps, with values the user enters.

rules: Write the steps as data and keep them in a memo, since onEnter runs each time its step shows.
Set intro: true on a welcome step for a wide centred panel; pass a Logo or BrandMark as art, and the mascot grows beside it.
An intro step shows Start the tour (goes on, holds focus) and Skip (ends the tour) instead of Back and Next; translate them with tour.introStart and tour.introSkip.
Give a step reveal when its target may not be drawn yet, such as a VirtualGrid item; call scrollToIndex there, and the tour finds the target after a frame.
Mark a target with data-tour and point at it with { tour }, or pass a ref; a step without a target sits in the middle.
Change the state of the app in onEnter, such as opening a panel or a tab, and make it safe to run twice; stop when its signal aborts.
Use advance: 'click' only when the click itself does what the step teaches; add clickTarget when one entry of the lit part goes on.
Use advance: 'wait' when the step ends on an event of the app, and call tour.next() from it; say what to do in hint.
Pass keep for parts that must stay usable all along, such as the title bar of the window.
Draw TourSpot in a second window that holds a target, such as a popped widget; it draws the spotlight only.
Treat placement as a wish: the bubble flips to the side that fits, stays in the window, or sits inside a hole that fills it.
Keep a tour short, five or six steps, with a title of a few words and a body of one or two lines.
Pass step and open with onStepChange and onOpenChange when the app must keep where the tour is.
a11y: The bubble is a dialog named by its title; focus moves to it on each step and goes back where it was on close.
A status line reads each step as Step 2 of 6 and the title.
The rest of the page is inert; the kept parts, the lit part of a click or wait step and its click target stay reachable.
Right or Enter goes on, Left goes back (not on an intro step) and Escape closes, ahead of the keys of the app; tour.shortcuts lists them.
A menu or popover opened during a step takes Escape first; the tour closes on the next press, before any dialog or screen.

The tour scrolls the target to the centre at once, through every scrolling ancestor, or to its top edge when it is taller than the window; then it measures the lit part each frame until it holds still.
With reduced motion the highlight and the mascot move at once and nothing fades.

path: a guided tour of the screen, one part at a time
tree.rule: GuidedTour lights one target per step, runs the step onEnter first, and lets the mascot walk beside the bubble, facing the target.

components.name: InfoScreen
components.job: An informational window to read, such as About or credits: a small dialog sized to its content and centred, with the title bar, the close button and one column.
useWhen: About the app, credits, a licence or a welcome page.
The user reads and changes nothing: the window has no tools.

avoidWhen.case: The screen holds settings or several pages.
The screen runs one short task with a status and actions.
The screen is one big custom surface.

rules: It opens small: the card fits its content, centred, at most 512 px wide, and only the column scrolls, once the window is too short for it.
Every informational window uses it, so About, credits and the like open at the same small size. A screen with tools is a WorkspaceScreen, a UtilityScreen or a StageScreen.
It has no page header and nothing adds one: the window title bar names it, and the column sits right under it.
Put a logo, the app name, a wordmark or a hero in lead, and the sections in the children.
List credits one entry per line; never widen the window for a grid of cards.
Put legal text in footer, never in the last section.
In a window under 560 px wide the card fills it and the column takes its width; lay out lead and sections so they wrap.
On an About screen, put the logo and the app name in lead and the build facts in a FactsPanel.
a11y: The card is a modal dialog named by the title.
Give each section a heading, so a screen reader can jump between them.

path: an informational window with no tools, such as About or credits
tree.rule: A small dialog sized to its content, one column to read.

components.name: InlineEdit
components.job: A piece of text that shows as text with a pen and turns into a field when the user clicks it, such as the title of a card.
useWhen: A short text is read far more than it is changed, so a field that is always open would clutter the view.
The user renames a title, a label or a note in place, on the page that shows it.

avoidWhen.case: The field belongs to a form that is filled in and sent.
The user creates a new thing from a name.
The text is Markdown that needs a toolbar and a preview.

rules: Own the text in the app: pass it as value, and set the new one in onCommit; the component keeps no copy once the edit ends.
Enter or leaving the field commits through onCommit, trimmed; text that did not change is not committed.
Escape cancels, restores the text and puts focus back on the text.
Click the text, or press Enter or F2 while it has focus, to start editing.
Pass validate to return a message for text that is not allowed; it shows under the field and nothing is committed until it returns nothing.
Pass multiline for a text area, where Enter adds a line and Mod+Enter commits.
Pass renderValue to draw the text when it is not edited, such as Markdown; the click, Enter and F2, and the name stay the same, and the field is unchanged.
A link or a control inside the drawn text does not start the edit when clicked; only a click on the rest of the text does.
Pass label to name the text for a screen reader, placeholder to stand in for an empty text, and disabled to show the text only.
a11y: The text is a button named Edit with the label and the text, and it says F2 in aria-keyshortcuts.
The field takes focus with its text selected, and it is named the same way as the button.
The message of validate is tied to the field, and the field is marked invalid while it shows.
A disabled text is a disabled button, so it is read but not offered for editing.

path: text shown as text, edited in place on click
tree.rule: InlineEdit starts, commits and cancels an edit in place with the same keys in every app.

components.name: ItemCard
components.job: One item of a catalogue as a card: media, a small line above the title, a status, the title, tags, details and its actions.
useWhen: A screen lists things to browse and pick from as a grid of cards, such as games in a store, mods or saves.
An overview shows a few areas side by side, each with a figure, a short summary and an action, with the media on the left.

avoidWhen.case: A box of content under a header row with its own actions.
Many items read as one line each, in a list.
One headline number with its change and a small chart.

rules: Keep the title to the name of the item, and put the source or the kind in eyebrow, such as Official.
Write details as short facts, such as World 1.2.0 and For AP 0.6.7; they join with dots and stop at three lines. Pass nodes too, such as a Tooltip around a status.
Give the main action kind primary; one other shows and the rest fold under More, danger ones asking first unless confirm is false.
Pass onOpen or href when the card opens a page of its own, and selected for the item open beside the list.
With href, pass navigate to route a plain click inside the app, as Link and SiteHeader take it.
Set mediaHeight auto when the media is a picture taller than the 96 px band, such as a 16 by 9 cover.
Set density compact for a long catalogue with no pictures: one row of about 56 px with the media as a 32 px tile, the title, one line and up to three icon actions.
Compact shows tags on a line of their own under the details, cut with a +N tag when they do not fit; give that row about 76 px.
In compact the details stay on one line and cut with an ellipsis, a Tooltip inside them still opens.
Set nameSuffix on each action of a row, such as the item name, so every Remove button has its own name.
Set confirm false on a danger action when the app asks with its own dialog; the card then does not ask first.
Set mediaSize sm to swap the 96 px band for a 32 px tile beside the title; compact does this itself.
In a VirtualList row, give the list a rowHeight of about 56 px (76 px with tags); the compact card fills the row width and sets no height of its own.
a11y: The title is a heading, level 3 by default, so a screen reader can jump from card to card.
With onOpen or href the title is the one button or link of the card; a click anywhere on the card goes through it, and the focus ring circles the card.
Compact actions are icon buttons whose label is their accessible name and their tooltip; give each action an icon.
The selected card marks its title with aria-current; the media is hidden from screen readers unless mediaLabel names it.
An action with nameSuffix reads as its label and the suffix, such as Remove Hollow Knight, in the button and its tooltip.

path: items of a catalogue, as cards
tree.rule: ItemCard gives every catalogue the same card, with its media, facts and actions in fixed places.

components.name: ItemList
components.job: The list side of a list and editor screen: a title with its count, New, a filter, groups, rename, delete and the loading, empty and error states.
useWhen: The user keeps a set of named things, such as presets, servers or profiles, and adds, renames, deletes and picks them.
The list loads from disk or the network, so it needs a loading line and an error in place of the rows.

avoidWhen.case: The list sits beside an editor whose edits can be lost when the user picks another item.
The rows are read only, or each row has its own set of actions.
The items need columns to sort, group and filter.

rules: Pass getId and getName; the name feeds the filter, the rename box and the labels of the row buttons.
Pass create to open a form at the top of the list, such as an InlineCreateForm with more fields, and call its close after a create or a cancel.
Pass onCreate in place of create when the app opens its own flow, such as a dialog or a wizard.
Pass createOpen with onCreateOpenChange when the app decides whether the form is open, such as on a first run with no items.
Pass newDisabled when New cannot run yet, with a string that says why, such as Start a game to make a new save; true greys it out with no reason.
Pass onActivate when picking an item acts at once, such as switching the active profile, and selectedId for the current one.
Pass showTitle={false} when a surrounding PanelContainer supplies the visible section heading; the list keeps its accessible name and any New action.
Pass onCount to learn the shown and total counts, such as to write the count into that PanelContainer heading; it runs after each change, with the filter and waiting deletes counted.
Pass groups with groupBy to set the order of the groups and keep the empty ones, such as an installed game with no preset yet.
An empty group draws its heading, its empty line and the button of its action, such as New preset; while the filter holds text, it hides.
Each row carries data-item-id with its id, so app search can find the row and scroll to it; rowData adds more data attributes.
New carries data-tour="item-list-new" for a GuidedTour step; pass createTour to tell two lists on one screen apart.
Leave actionVisibility on hover to show rename and delete on the picked row and on any row under the pointer; always shows them on every row.
Pass rowActions for buttons of your own before rename and delete, such as Load; give each the tabIndex it receives so the row keeps one Tab stop.
Pass undoDelete, such as 8000, when a delete should run at once: the row turns into Deleted with Undo, and onDelete runs when the time is up.
Write onDelete as the delete for good when undoDelete is set; it also runs for a row still waiting when the list unmounts.
Each waiting delete joins the one undo stack of useUndo, so Ctrl+Z in the list undoes it in turn with the toasts that carry undo.
Pass deleteKey to bind the Delete key on a focused row: with undoDelete it deletes at once, without it it opens the Delete question.
Return media from render, such as a save screenshot, to draw it flush on the left of the row at the full row height; mediaWidth or mediaAspect sets its width.
Pass maxRows, such as 6, to show that many rows and scroll the rest; the title, count, New and filter stay above the scroll area.
maxRows counts rows, not group headings: a grouped list shows the headings between its first rows inside the height.
Pass renameInline with onRename to rename in place: a pen shows next to the name on hover or focus, and the name turns into a field inside the row in place of the separate rename button.
Keep the meta of each row to one short line, such as 7 changes · edited 2 hours ago.
Write empty as what to do next, such as Install a game from Games, then make a preset for it.
Pass the raw failure as error, such as an Error or its message: the list shows Could not load followed by its title, with the raw text behind Details.
Pass onRetry with error to add a Retry button, and set loading while the new try runs.
Put it on a surface: the list pane of ListDetailLayout, a card or a panel. It draws no background of its own.
a11y: The list is a section named by its title, and each group is a list named by its heading.
The arrow keys, Home and End move the selection between rows, or only the focus with onActivate; F2 renames the focused row.
With onActivate the rows are one Tab stop on the focused row; a click, Enter or Space activates it, and Tab reaches its actions.
An empty group is a group named by its heading; its action is a Tab stop of its own, and the arrow keys skip it.
In the rename box, Enter keeps the name and Escape cancels; focus goes back to the row.
New moves focus into the create form; Escape or Cancel closes it and focus goes back to New.
After a create, focus goes to the new row when the app picks it, and back to New when it does not.
Delete asks once with its own Cancel, and the error is an alert.
With undoDelete, Undo is a status with its own Tab stop; Ctrl+Z in the list undoes the latest step, and the time waits under the pointer or focus.
A New that is off with a reason stays a Tab stop marked disabled; its reason is its description and shows on hover and focus.
After the Delete key, focus and the selection move to the next row; after the trash button, focus goes to Undo, and after Undo back to the row.

path: a list the user adds to, renames and deletes from
tree.rule: ItemList draws the count, New, the filter, the groups, rename, delete and every state of such a list the same way in every app.

components.name: JobDialog
components.job: A long job in a dialog: its TaskProgress, with Cancel and Hide while it runs and Close once it ends.
useWhen: The user starts a long job, such as a generation, an install or an update, and should see it run.
The user may hide the job and go on working, then come back to it.

avoidWhen.case: The progress belongs in a page or a panel, not over it.
The dialog asks a question and waits for the answer.

rules: Name the job in the title, such as Generating Friday async, and keep it while the job runs.
Keep the job running when the dialog hides, and give the user a way back to it, such as a button with the percent.
Pass onCancel only when the job can stop; set cancelling while it stops.
Add Try again through actions after a failure, beside Close.
Mark the dialog with id and data, such as data-job-id, to find it from the app; both go on the element with role dialog.
a11y: Focus starts on Hide while the job runs and on Close once it ends.
Escape hides a running job and closes an ended one, as the close button does.
The progress inside reads as TaskProgress does: a status word, a named bar and an alert on failure.

path: a long job the user can hide or cancel
tree.rule: JobDialog puts TaskProgress in a dialog whose buttons follow the state of the job.

components.name: KanbanBoard
components.job: A board of cards in named columns, such as tasks by state, where the user drags a card within a column or to another one.
useWhen: Items move through a few named stages, such as todo, doing, review and done, and the user sorts them by hand.
The app names the columns and owns the cards; the board draws them and reports each move.
Each column may fold to a narrow rail, so the user can keep a long board in view.

avoidWhen.case: The items are one flat list the user reorders, with no stages.
The user browses, sorts or filters many records in rows and columns.
The cards are catalogue items with media and facts, laid out in a grid.

rules: Pass columns as { id, title, cards } where each card has an id; the app decides the columns and nothing is fixed.
Keep the columns in the app: onMove gets { cardId, from, to } with a columnId and an index each, and the app changes its data.
Read to.index as the place the card has after the move, in its new column; moveCard applies a move to the columns for you.
Draw the inside of a card with renderCard, such as a title and tag badges; the board draws the frame and the grip.
Pass cardLabel to name a card in the grip and in the announcement; it falls back to the card id.
Pass cardEdgeTone to draw a coloured edge on some cards, such as danger for a card that needs the user; return undefined for a card with no edge.
Give the board a height, such as a flex child or a fixed block size: each column scrolls on its own and the board scrolls sideways.
Set columnWidth to fill so the columns share the board width instead of a fixed width; each keeps a minimum, and the board scrolls sideways when the minimums do not fit.
Put a badge after the count of a column header, such as 2 quiet, with badge on the column; put a control at the header end, such as an Add button, with action.
Both are drawn from the column data, so a column that has neither looks as before; a folded column hides its action and keeps its badge on the rail.
Put a form or a control above the cards, such as an inline add form, with top on the column; it is not a card, so it takes no drag slot, and a folded column hides it.
Fold columns with collapsed and onCollapsedChange, or let defaultCollapsed start them folded; both take column ids.
a11y: The board and each column are named groups, and each column holds a named list of cards.
The grip is a button on each card: drag it, or press Up and Down to move within the column and Left and Right to move to the next column.
Keys skip a folded column, and focus stays on the moved card.
Each move is announced in a polite live region with the card, the column and the place, such as Fix login moved to Doing, position 2 of 4.
Every control is at least 24 pixels, and the fold button names its column and says if it is expanded.

path: cards in columns the user drags between, such as tasks by state
tree.rule: KanbanBoard keeps the move, the keys, the counts and the fold the same in every board, so an app only draws its cards.

components.name: KeyValueEditor
components.job: A map of names to values, row by row: a name, a value control and Remove, then an add row, with a check for names listed twice.
useWhen: An option is a map, such as item counts for a start inventory, and a raw JSON box would let one typo break it.
The names come from a list of valid items, or are typed freely, and each has a number, a word or a choice.

avoidWhen.case: The value nests deeper than one name and one value.
The value is a set of names with nothing attached.

rules: Pass keys whenever the valid names are known, so the add row searches them and a wrong name is caught.
Pick valueKind for the values: count for small whole numbers, number, text or select with options.
Store the value from onChange; it waits while a name is empty, listed twice or not in keys.
Pass onProblem to hold the Save of the form: it gets the problem while a row is wrong, and null once it is fixed.
a11y: The editor is a group named by its Field or FormRow label, or by aria-label, and its rows are a list.
Each value control is named Value of and the name, and each Remove button Remove and the name.
A problem is an alert under the rows, and the rows it is about are marked invalid.

path: pairs of a name and a value
tree.rule: KeyValueEditor edits a map row by row and holds it back while it has a duplicate, the same way in every app.

components.name: ListDetail
components.job: An ItemList beside the editor of the picked item, that asks before a pick, New or Back throws unsaved edits away.
useWhen: A screen lists saved things on the left and edits the picked one on the right, such as presets or servers.
The editor holds edits until the user saves, so moving away must ask first.

avoidWhen.case: The detail is read only, or every edit saves at once.
Only the list is needed, with no editor beside it.

rules: Set dirty from the editor: true while its value differs from the saved one.
Pass onSave so the question offers Save and open; return false, or reject, when the save fails.
Pass onDiscard to throw the draft away; onSelect runs after it.
Keep the list props in list; ListDetail adds the selection and guards New, with create or onCreate.
New asks before a create form in list opens, and opens it after Discard or a save that worked; picking the new item is up to the app.
Pass onActivate in list when a pick also acts; another row asks first, like a pick, and the arrow keys then move only the focus.
The action of a group in list asks first too, like New.
With createOpen in list, New reaches onCreateOpenChange only after the answer; a createOpen the app sets on its own skips the question.
The question is a bar over the editor by default; pass guard dialog to ask in a modal dialog instead.
Put a SaveBar at the foot of the editor, for Save and Discard while the user stays on the item.
Every prop of ListDetailLayout passes through, such as storageKey, collapsed and emptyDetail; detail shows only while an item is picked.
a11y: The question takes focus on Keep editing, and Escape stays; focus goes back where it was, such as to New.
By default the question is an alertdialog over the editor; with guard dialog it is a modal dialog.
The list keeps every key of ItemList; the panes keep every key of ListDetailLayout, with Enter on the divider to fold the list.

path: a list beside an editor, with unsaved edits guarded
tree.rule: ListDetail joins ItemList and ListDetailLayout and asks the same question before edits are lost in every app.

components.name: ListDetailLayout
components.job: The two panes of a list and detail screen: the list on the left and the detail of the picked item beside it, each on its own surface.
useWhen: A screen lists things on the left and shows the picked one on the right, such as sessions, servers or saves.
The user needs more room for the detail now and then, so the list folds away to a rail.
A table beside a wide detail shares the room by ratio, and the detail folds away to give the table the whole width.

avoidWhen.case: The detail is an editor whose edits can be lost when the user picks another item.
Two panes of equal weight split the room by share.
The left side is the navigation of the app.

rules: Pass listContainers with titled sections and the detail as content; the layout draws the panes, their surfaces and their scroll.
Each list container keeps its required primary heading. The list pane title comes from listLabel by default; pass listShowTitle={false} when the section title is sufficient.
Pass listAction and listRailItems for the list pane action and folded rail icons. The detail pane keeps its generic editor content.
Leave detail out, or pass null, while nothing is picked; emptyDetail replaces the default placeholder.
Pass onBack to clear the selection; under 768 px it shows the list again.
Pass storageKey to keep the width and the fold between visits; the fold is kept under storageKey:collapsed.
Pass collapsed with onCollapsedChange when the app holds the fold, such as from a menu or its own shortcut.
Pass listRatio, such as 0.6, to give the list a share of the room in place of a width in pixels; the divider then drags the share, from 0.2 to 0.8.
Pass detailCollapsible to let the detail fold to a rail the same way, or detailCollapsed with onDetailCollapsedChange to hold it.

The divider always resizes; pulling the list about 32 px narrower than its minimum folds it to a rail, and dragging the rail outward opens it. With detailCollapsible, pulling the divider past the largest list folds the detail the same way.
Pass listScroll={false} or detailScroll={false} when the content scrolls by itself, such as a DataTable or a tab strip over its own scroll area; each list container then fills the pane.
Put a SaveBar last in the detail: it sits flush with the foot of the pane.
Name the panes with listLabel and detailLabel, in lower case, such as presets and preset editor.

A folded pane is the rail of SidePanel, drawn by the same part: sunken, 60 px wide, its label written sideways, reading up on the left and down on the right. The fold buttons overlap the dashed outside border, with the list button on its detail side and the detail button on its list side.

The primary list border stays visible while its rail is folded, and its chevron stays centered on the border at the heading row. When both panes can fold, the detail chevron sits just below the list chevron on that same border so both controls remain usable. Pixel-width list folding animates the pane tracks and rail; ratio layouts and detail folding settle directly to the rail width. Motion is disabled for reduced-motion preferences.
a11y: The dashed outside border is also the resize separator: the arrow keys resize it, Home and End jump to the limits, Space and a double click reset it.
Enter on the divider, or an arrow key at the end of the range, folds the list and moves focus to the button that brings it back; Enter or the outward arrow key on a folded divider opens it.
The fold button is the CollapseToggle: it names the list, Hide presets or Show presets, and reports aria-expanded on the list pane.
The detail fold button names the detail the same way, Hide preset editor or Show preset editor, on the detail pane.
Under 768 px the panes stack and Back sits at the top of the detail.

tree.rule: ListDetailLayout draws the panes, the resize, the fold and the small window of every list and detail screen the same way.

components.name: LoadError
components.job: What to show when something fails to load: one plain sentence, a Retry button and the raw error behind Details.
useWhen: A list, a screen or a section could not load its data, such as the server list or the sessions page.
A choice could not load its options, such as the sound devices in a settings row.

avoidWhen.case: The load worked and there is nothing to show.
A long job with steps and a log failed.
A part threw while it rendered.

rules: Write message as one plain sentence that says what failed, such as Could not load your servers; never the raw error.
Pass the raw failure as error, an Error, a string or an object: it waits behind Details, closed, so the user can copy it into a report.
Pass onRetry when the load can run again, and set retrying while it runs so the button spins and takes no second click.
Use variant center to fill a list pane or a screen, box inside a section, and inline in a row.
ItemList, ErrorBoundary and SettingsRow draw it from their own props; reach for it directly in other places.
a11y: The sentence is an alert, so a screen reader reads it once when the load fails.
Details is the browser details element, and the raw text scrolls by keyboard once it takes focus.

path: something failed to load, with Retry
tree.rule: LoadError draws every failed load the same way: a sentence, Retry and the raw error behind Details.

components.name: LogPanel
components.job: A running log, such as a server log or a simulation trace, in one framed box with search, filters, a line count and Copy all.
useWhen: Lines arrive over time and the user reads, searches and filters them, such as a server log or the trace of a run.
The user picks some lines to copy or act on, such as the lines to attach to a bug report.

avoidWhen.case: The rows have columns to sort and resize.
A job shows its steps, with a short log under them.
The text is code or a fixed block to read and copy.

rules: Give each row a stable id: the window, the new line behaviour and the selection all follow it.
Pass kinds with a tone per type: a text tone, a tag tint such as teal, or an app hex colour, lifted until it reads.
A line takes the tone of its kind; set tone on one row to colour that line alone, with or without a kind.
Set toneMessage to colour the message in the same tone, as for errors, or to a tone of its own, such as dim.
Set strong on a kind whose messages mark a step, such as a session that starts, and uppercase to set them in capitals.
Pass selectedIds with onSelectionChange to let the user pick rows; the app holds the set and copies or acts on it.
Put the action on the picked rows in toolbarExtra, such as Copy selected or Report these lines, beside the line count.
Set ansi for lines that carry colour codes, such as a build or process output; other escape codes are stripped, never drawn.
ansi draws the sixteen colours, bold, dim, italic and underline; 256 and true colour map to the nearest of the sixteen.
Follow is on: the view stays at the end while lines arrive, and a scroll up stops it until Jump to bottom is pressed.
Set order="newest-first" to show the latest line at the top; follow then sticks to the top and Jump to top returns to it.
Set follow={false} to leave the view where the reader put it; set onInput to add a prompt row for a process that reads lines.
onInput gets each line on Enter; Up and Down walk the lines sent. Echo the line back as a row yourself.
Return false, or a promise that resolves false or rejects, to keep the text in the field and out of the history; true or nothing clears it.
While a returned promise is pending a second Enter is ignored, so one line is never sent twice.
Set inputDisabled to show the row with a disabled field even when onInput is absent, and inputPlaceholder to say why, such as This run has no input.
Pass height="fill" inside a box that sets the height, or a number for a fixed height in pixels.
a11y: Without a selection the log is one focusable region that the arrow keys scroll.
With selectedIds the rows are options of a listbox: Up and Down move the pick, Shift extends it, and a click with Shift picks the rows between.
The input row is a labelled text field; the prompt mark is hidden from screen readers.
Each time cell carries the review mask, so screenshots of a running log compare run to run.

tree.rule: LogPanel shows a running log with search, filters, the newest lines first in view and rows the user can pick.

components.name: Markdown
components.job: Shows a Markdown text, such as the release note of a version, as formatted text drawn with Tessera parts: headings, paragraphs, lists, task lists, tables, bold, italic, strikethrough, links, inline code, code blocks, quotes and rules. Raw HTML is dropped.
useWhen: The app shows a release note written in Markdown, in an update dialog or an about page.
The text comes as Markdown from a file or a server and the app only shows it.
A game or project README with tables and task lists.

avoidWhen.case: The text is written in the app itself.
The text is code to show as it is.

rules: Pass the Markdown as children or as source; the part keeps no state.
Every piece is drawn with a Tessera part, never styled HTML: Text for headings, Link, List and ListItem, Table, Checkbox, Code, Strong, Em, S, BlockQuote, CodeBlock and Divider.
GitHub tables, task lists, strikethrough and autolinks are on. A table is a Table, so it matches every other table in the app.
A task item (- [x] done, - [ ] to do) is a read-only Checkbox, disabled, with the item text as its label; the box follows the source and the user cannot tick it.
Write each release note as release-notes/v<version>.md: a # <Product> v<version> title, a summary paragraph, ## sections and plain bullets.
Set headingOffset so the headings sit under the heading of the place: 1, the default, makes # an h2.
Set hideTitle when the frame around the note already names the version, such as the notes box of a UtilityScreen.
Set size sm in a dialog or a notes box.
Set size inline inside a card or an InlineEdit display: no block margins, paragraphs as runs, tight lists, and headings as bold text at the text size.
Pass onLink in a desktop app to open a link in the system browser; without it a link opens in a new tab.
Only http, https and mailto links are kept. Any other link and raw HTML become plain text or nothing, and an image shows its alt text.
Pass images to draw images: true allows http and https addresses, and a function gets each src and returns the address to load, or nothing to drop the image.
An image is drawn with Image, with its alt text, lazy loading and no wider than the text; it stays off by default.
With images on, base64 data images of type png, jpeg, gif and webp are drawn too, up to 2 million characters; svg and every other data type are always dropped.
Pass onImage to make each drawn image a button, focusable and pressed with Enter or Space, named by its alt text; it gets { src, alt }, so the app can open a lightbox. Without it images stay inert.
Control characters (except tab and line breaks), private-use characters and lone surrogates are removed from the source before it is parsed; emoji and normal text stay.
Pass linkIds, a rule or a list of rules with a pattern and an href function, so plain ids such as T-5 become links; they are made in text only, never in code or inside a link.
A link that starts with a slash, such as /files/notes.md, is an app path: it is kept only when onLink is passed, and goes to onLink like any link.

Whatever an href function gives still has to be an http, https or mailto address, or an app path with onLink; javascript addresses are always dropped, and data addresses only pass as the image types above.
a11y: Headings keep their order, moved down by headingOffset, so a screen reader can jump between sections.
A link that opens a new tab says so in its label.
Lists are real lists, read with their length and position.
A table is a real table with a head, so each cell is read with its column heading.
A task item is a disabled Checkbox that a screen reader reads as checked or not checked, with its text as the name.

path: formatted text from Markdown, such as release notes
tree.rule: Markdown shows a Markdown text drawn with Tessera parts, with raw HTML and unsafe links dropped.

components.name: MarkdownEditor
components.job: A multi-line field for writing Markdown, with a toolbar for bold, italic, lists, quotes, links and code, and a live preview drawn by Markdown.
useWhen: The user writes a note, a description or a release text that is stored as Markdown.
The user should see how the text will look while they write it.

avoidWhen.case: The text is plain, with no formatting.
The app only shows a Markdown text and nobody edits it.
The text is structured data, such as JSON.

rules: Own the text in the app and pass it as value, with onChange; the editor keeps no copy of it.
Leave layout out to get split on a wide container and Write and Preview tabs on a narrow one.
Set layout to split to keep both panes, which stack under a narrow container, or to tabs to keep the preview behind its tab.
Pass onLink in a desktop app so a link in the preview opens in the system browser.
Pass images and linkIds, the same as for Markdown, so the preview draws images and links ids the way the saved note will; with a slash path, onLink is needed too.
Pass compact for a note box inside a card: a slim toolbar, a 3 row textarea that grows with its text up to a cap, and no split or tabs; rows still sets the starting height.
In compact the preview stays out until the Preview button at the end of the toolbar is pressed; it then takes the place of the text, and a second press brings the text back.
Pass label, hint, error, placeholder and disabled as for any other field; set rows to change the height of the text, 12 by default.
The toolbar acts on the selection: it wraps it, or puts a prefix on each line it touches, and a second press removes the mark.
Enter at the end of a list item starts the next one: a bullet, a number that counts up, or an open task; on an empty item it ends the list.
Tab indents a list line by two spaces and Shift+Tab takes them back; outside a list Tab moves the focus as usual.
Backspace right after an empty marker removes the marker; typing - [] and a space makes a task item.
The Quote button puts "> " before each line the selection touches, and a second press removes it.
Pass autoFocus to put the caret at the end of the text when the editor appears; on the tabs layout the Write tab shows first.
Mod+B is bold, Mod+I is italic and Mod+K is a link, shown in the tooltip of each button.
Pass onSubmit to send the text on Mod+Enter; it gets the current value.
Pass onEscape to leave the editor on Escape; it is not called while a menu or popover is open, or when another part has taken the key.
Pass maxLength to stop the text at that length; a counter shows in the last 10 percent of the limit, such as 95 / 100.
Edits go through the browser, so Undo and Redo keep working after a toolbar button.
a11y: The toolbar is a toolbar with a name, and every button is named by a word, never by its icon alone.
A button with a shortcut says it in its tooltip and in aria-keyshortcuts.
The tabs are real tabs; the toolbar is off while the preview is shown.
The preview is a region named Preview, so a screen reader can jump to it.

path: Markdown text, with a live preview
tree.rule: MarkdownEditor writes Markdown with a toolbar and a live preview, the same way in every app.

components.name: MarqueeBox
components.job: The rectangle that shows an area being dragged over items to pick them, drawn inside the box that scrolls.
useWhen: The user drags over a grid of tiles, files or marks to pick the ones inside, as in a file manager.
The rectangle comes from useMarqueeSelect and must follow the pointer while the box scrolls.

avoidWhen.case: The user picks rows of a table with checkboxes or clicks.
The user moves an item or resizes a window by dragging.

rules: Pass the rect of useMarqueeSelect; it is null when nobody drags, and then nothing is drawn.
Place it inside the box that scrolls, and give that box position relative, so the rectangle moves with the content.
Spread bind of the hook on that same box, and mark each item with data-marquee-key.
It takes no pointer events, so the items below keep their hover and focus.
a11y: The rectangle is decoration and hidden from readers; the picked items must show their own selected state.
Dragging is not the only way to pick: give the items keys or checkboxes for the same choice.

path: a rectangle dragged over items to pick them
tree.rule: MarqueeBox draws the rectangle of a drag to pick, with the border and fill of the theme.

components.name: MediaViewer
components.job: Opens a picture or a video large over the page in a dialog, with zoom by steps, a Fit and actual size switch, dragging to look around, and arrows through a set.
useWhen: A small picture of a file, a store item or a save opens large when the user presses it or an Expand button.
A sprite or a sprite sheet is looked at closely, pixel by pixel.

avoidWhen.case: The picture stays in the page.
The video stays in the page, with theatre mode and full screen.
Slides turn in the page itself.

rules: Pass items as id, kind image or video, src and name; the name is the title of the dialog.
Pass index and onIndexChange, or defaultIndex, to open on the item the user pressed.
Draw the small picture with Expand as a recipe: an Image in a Pressable and a Button that set open.
Pass startAt in seconds when a small video preview was playing, so the large one starts where it stopped.
Leave pixelated on auto: pictures of 256 pixels or less on their longest side stay sharp; pass true or false to force it.
The small picture takes the same pixelated on Image, so a sprite looks the same before and after it opens.
a11y: It is a DialogShell named by the item name: Escape and the close button close it, and focus goes back to what opened it.
The zoom buttons, the minus and plus keys, and 0 for Fit work from anywhere in the dialog; the Left and Right keys move through a set.
The place in a set, such as 2 of 6, is a polite live region.

path: a picture or a video opened large, with zoom
tree.rule: MediaViewer opens a picture or a video large in a dialog, with zoom, dragging and arrows through a set.

components.name: PanelContainer
components.job: A plain stacked section with a heading, optional action and a body.
useWhen: A side pane needs a consistently headed section.
A list or detail pane needs the shared panel heading and body structure.

avoidWhen.case: Content needs a card surface, outline or interactive state.

rules: Pass title for the heading and children for the body.
The title is always shown above the body without a card surface or border.
Pass action for a control in the header.
Pass fill to take the room left in a flex column; the body then has a definite height, so a DataTable inside scrolls on its own.
a11y: The title is a heading; the body remains arbitrary content.
components.example:
import { PanelContainer } from '@drizztdourden08/tessera';

<PanelContainer title="Profiles" action="New">
  Profiles go here.
</PanelContainer>

components.name: PathInput
components.job: A file or folder path the user can type, drop from the desktop or pick with Browse in one box, with copy, reveal and clear.
useWhen: A setting holds the path of a file or a folder, such as an SSH key, a ROM, a save folder or an output zip.
The app shows a path it made, read only, and the user may copy it or open its folder.

avoidWhen.case: The app needs the contents of the files, not their path.
The value is free text that is not a path.

rules: Pass onBrowse to open the dialog of the app, such as the native dialog through Electron, and return the picked path or null.
Pass resolvePath in Electron, such as webUtils.getPathForFile, so a drop gives the full path and not only the name.
Set kind and accept to what the setting takes, so a wrong drop is turned away with a reason.
Pass onReveal only when the app can show the file in its folder.
Pass onBlur to check or save a typed path when the user leaves the box, as on a TextInput.
a11y: The input takes the label, hint and error of its Field, and typing edits the path.
Copy, Reveal, Clear and Browse are buttons with names, in that order after the input.
A drop that is turned away marks the input invalid and says why in an alert under it.
A file dragged in from the desktop marks the box as a drop target at once, before the drop.

path: a path to a file or folder
tree.rule: PathInput takes a typed, dropped or browsed path in one box and cuts a long one in the middle, the same way in every app.

components.name: Rating
components.job: A row of stars that shows how well something is rated, to the nearest half star, with the number and the count; with onChange it is the picker a person rates with.
useWhen: A store card, an item page or a list shows the average rating of a pack, a preset or a world.
A person gives their own rating, such as Your rating on an item page.

avoidWhen.case: The number is picked on a track, such as a volume.
One of a few named options is picked.
A label sits beside a value that is not a score.

rules: Pass the average as value; pass null when nobody has rated yet, never 0, so the stars fade and read Not rated yet.
Pass count for the number of ratings and showValue for the average beside the stars, such as 4.6 (212).
Pass onChange to make it the picker; value is then the whole star the person picked, or null before they pick.
Set disabled on the picker while a rating is being saved.
Use size sm on cards and in rows, md in running text and lg in a ratings panel or for the picker.
Build a ratings panel from Card, ProgressBar, Rating and a Button: the panel is a recipe, not a part.
a11y: A shown rating is one image with one sentence, such as 4.6 out of 5, from 212 ratings.
The picker is a radio group with a radio per star and one Tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End move and pick.
label names the picker, Your rating by default, and prefixes the sentence of a shown rating.

path: a status, a count or a label
a score in stars, or a rating to give
tree.rule: Rating shows an average in half stars with its count, and with onChange is the star picker.

components.name: ResizeHandle
components.job: The one thin line between two panels that the user drags, or moves with the keys, to resize the panel beside it, and that folds the panel when pulled past the end of its range.
useWhen: A side panel keeps its own width in pixels and the user drags its edge to change it, such as an outline or an inspector.
A part draws its own panes and needs the one resize line every Tessera layout draws.

avoidWhen.case: Two panes share the room by ratio and one can fold behind a rail.
A list sits beside the detail of the picked item.
The user moves panels around and docks them.

rules: Pair it with usePaneSize and spread its handle: the hook keeps the size, its limits and storageKey, and the handle wires the line.
Size the panel from usePaneSize size, as an inline width: the line moves nothing by itself.
For a side panel, a list beside its detail or two panes, draw the edge with SidePanel, ListDetailLayout or SplitPane: they put the fold button beside this line for you.
Pass edge="end" for a panel after the line, such as an inspector on the right, so dragging toward it shrinks it.
Pass orientation="vertical" for panes stacked one above the other; the line then lies across and moves up and down.
It draws one line, a thin --c-border-strong that brightens a little to --c-text-muted on hover, focus and drag; there is no other look.

Pass fold when the panel can fold: { sides, folded, onFold, onUnfold }. A drag past the end of the range by about 32 px, or an arrow key at the end, calls onFold; dragging out from a folded panel, or the opposite arrow key, calls onUnfold with the value to open at.
Enter folds an open panel and opens a folded one, and onReset still runs on Space and a double click.
a11y: It is a focusable separator with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax; name the panel in label, such as Resize outline.
Pass controls with the id of the panel it resizes, for aria-controls.
The arrow keys move it by step, Shift by largeStep, and Home and End jump to the limits; at the end of the range an arrow key folds the panel when fold allows it.
While a panel is folded the value reads as zero, and the minimum reads as zero when the panel can fold.

path: a side panel the user drags wider
tree.rule: ResizeHandle is the one resize line of every Tessera layout: drag, keys, value, range and drag to fold, with usePaneSize to keep a width in pixels.

components.name: RetryButton
components.job: Tries a failed step again, such as a lost connection or a failed fetch, and counts down to the next automatic try.
useWhen: A connection closed or failed and the user can start it again.
The app tries again by itself after a wait and the user should see how long, or skip the wait.

avoidWhen.case: The action is not a second try of something that failed.
The failure belongs to a long job with steps and a log.

rules: Keep the timer in the app: pass retryAt, the time of the next automatic try, and start that try from the app, never from the button.
Pass attempt and attempts only when the app stops after a fixed number of tries.
Set retrying while a try runs, so the button shows a spinner and takes no second click.
Put it at the end of the row that says what failed, with the reason in the text before it.
a11y: The button is named Retry, or Retry now while a countdown runs.
The countdown line describes the button, so it is read on focus and not every second.

tree.rule: RetryButton says how long until the next automatic try and lets the user skip the wait, with one look for every retry.

components.name: RowGrid
components.job: A short list the user edits in place, one row per item and one input per column, such as the players of a session.
useWhen: Each item has the same few fields, and the user adds, removes and reorders the items.
The list is short, tens of rows at most, and every row stays editable.

avoidWhen.case: The user browses, sorts or picks from many records.
Each item has many fields or a nested shape.
Each row is a name and one value of a map.
The rows are read only with a few actions.

rules: Give each column a min and a max in pixels; the grid stays a table while every min fits.
Mark the least needed column fold, so it moves to a second line before the rows turn into cards.
Put the field that names the row first: in cards it heads the card.
Keep the rows in the app and change them in onAdd, onRemove and onMove; the grid only draws them.
Pass error per column as a sentence that says how to fix it.
Pass selectedKey for the row the app has open, such as the row whose Edit button is pressed; the app keeps it.
a11y: Each row is a group named after rowLabel, and each input is named by its column; the selected row carries aria-current.
Ctrl and Up or Down moves to the same column in the row above or below.
The grip moves its row with Up and Down; the row menu has Move up and Move down too.
Adding, removing and moving a row is announced, and focus lands on the next useful control.

path: a short list of items with the same few fields
tree.rule: RowGrid edits a short list row by row, a table when wide and cards when narrow, the same way in every app.

components.name: SaveBar
components.job: The bar at the foot of an editor: whether its edits are saved, the reason a save failed, and Save and Discard.
useWhen: A screen edits one thing, such as a preset or a session, and keeps the edits until the user saves.
The user needs to see at a glance whether the edits are saved, and to save or drop them from one place.

avoidWhen.case: Each setting applies the moment it changes.
A new thing is named before it exists.
The edits are steps of one task with Back and Next.

rules: Put the bar last in the editor, so it stays at the foot of the scrolling area.
Move state through clean, dirty, saving, then saved or error; the app owns it and the bar only draws it.
Pass error as a sentence that says what to do, such as Free some space and save again.
Pass onDiscard to offer Discard; leave it out when the edits cannot be dropped.
a11y: The save state is a status region, so a screen reader hears Saving, Saved or Not saved with the reason.
Save and Discard are off while there is nothing to save, and Save shows a spinner while it saves.

path: whether the edits are saved, with Save and Discard
tree.rule: SaveBar says whether an editor is saved and holds Save and Discard at its foot, the same way in every app.

components.name: ScreenLayer
components.job: Building block: the overlay and the card of every screen, with one gap around the card that follows the room.
useWhen: You build a new kind of screen that none of the screen kinds or ScreenWindow can hold.

avoidWhen.case: You show a screen with pages and a side list.
You show About, credits or another screen to read.
You show one short task with a status, such as an update check.
You show one big custom surface, such as calibration.
You need a title, a close button and an empty container.

rules: Use it only inside a screen kind. App code shows screens through the kinds.
Put it in a positioned parent: it covers that parent, usually the whole app.
Never set a margin or a padding on the gap: the layer works it out from its room.
Draw the inside of the card yourself, including its padding, which is the same on all four sides.
Use size="compact" for a card that fits its content, up to a readable width.
Use size="info" for an informational window with no tools: a small card that fits its content, centred, up to 512 px wide. InfoScreen sets it.
Set square for a window shown fullscreen: the card drops its corner radius and its outer border, and the host draws what surrounds it.
Pass corner for small round buttons on the top right corner of the card, half over its edge, such as the X of a window with no title row.
Set tight for a window with no title row: the gap around the card takes the next smaller space token at every size.

Pass move to let the user move the card by its top edge and resize it from its edges and corners: rect is where it sits, null for its snapped spot, and onChange gets each new rect. The card stays inside the layer, floating and corner included, and no smaller than min.
a11y: The card and the floating switcher are one modal dialog. Pass labelledBy with the id of a visible title, or label when there is none.
On open focus moves to the labelledBy title, or to the first control without one; Tab stays inside, and on close focus returns to the opener.
While open, the siblings of the layer in its parent are inert: put the page it covers beside it, and keep a title bar outside that parent.
hidden takes the layer out of the page and out of the accessibility tree, and keeps its content mounted.
Pass onClose and Escape calls it, after every menu, popover and dialog above the layer; a hidden layer takes no Escape.
floating comes before the card in the page order, so a switcher in it is the first Tab stop; it still draws on the top edge of the card.
corner comes after floating, and the Move window handle of move after corner, both before the card.

components.name: ScreenPage
components.job: Building block: the page header container WorkspaceScreen and StageScreen show, a card with a header of icon, title and fading backdrop over a body that compacts the header once it scrolls.
useWhen: You build a new kind of screen and it must look like the others, with the same header.
A page in an app frame needs the same header as the pages of a screen.

avoidWhen.case: The screen has pages the user moves between from a side list.
The screen is read, such as About or credits.
The screen runs one short task with a status and actions.
The screen is one big custom surface.
The page holds settings with a pill per section.
Only the header, on a card or a panel of your own.

rules: WorkspaceScreen and StageScreen render it, and neither can turn it off. UtilityScreen shows its header at the top of the window instead, and InfoScreen has none.
Always pass an icon and a title; without them it warns in development.
Leave backdrop out for the default art, pass your own scene, or pass null for a plain header. For an image or a colour, pass a BackdropLayer.
Use strip for a few controls after the title, such as section pills or a status, and actions for the end of the header.
On a sub-page, pass back with the name of the parent page and what returns to it; the header draws Back to and that name before the icon.
Put buttons that stay in view in footer; the body scrolls between the header and the footer.
Set scroll={false} when the content scrolls by itself; the header then stays full size.

The header stays one row while its parts fit beside the whole title; a HeaderAnchorNav strip takes the room left and scrolls sideways. Short of room it stacks: the strip moves to a row of its own under the title, and actions follow when the title needs the room. Never hide the strip yourself for a narrow window.
a11y: The card is a section named by its title, which is a level 2 heading.
With live, a screen reader reads each new title, as a status does.

components.name: ScreenWindow
components.job: Building block: the plain screen window, a ScreenLayer with a title bar, a page header or only corner buttons at its top, a close button and an empty container.
useWhen: You build a new kind of screen on the window every screen kind shares.
A screen fits none of the four kinds and needs only a title, a close button and its own content.

avoidWhen.case: The screen has pages the user moves between from a side list.
The screen is read, such as About or credits.
The screen runs one short task with a status and actions.
The screen is one big custom surface.

rules: Reach for a screen kind first. Use ScreenWindow alone only when none of them fits.
The title bar is the default top. Pass header to make a ContentHeader the top edge of the window instead: title is its title, and the close button sits at the end of its actions.
With header the window has no padding and no card inside: the children pad themselves, so a scrolling body reaches the window edge.
With header, subtitle and extra do not show; put such controls in header.strip or header.actions.
Pass back to draw a back button before the title, in the title bar or in the page header, for a screen opened from another one. The host wires Alt+Left and the mouse back button to the same call.
With the title row, the padding inside the card is the same on all four sides. Never add padding around the children to make up for it.

Pass titleRow={false} for a card or a hub with no title row: the title row goes, the title sits in a small chip half over the top left corner of the card, and a round X sits half over the top right corner.

The corner chip has the height, surface, border and shadow of the round X, with small dim text. Pass icon for a 14 px glyph before the title. A long title ends in an ellipsis before it reaches the buttons on the right.

The chip adds no height and never a row inside the content. Pass cornerTitle={false} to keep the corner bare, for example when a floating switch already names the screen: the chip goes and the title only names the dialog.

With titleRow={false}, pass the title as plain text, keep back for windows with a title row, and expect a tighter window: a smaller gap around the card, lg padding on the sides and bottom, and 8 px between the switch and the content.

Pass movable with titleRow={false} to add a lock left of the X. Locked, the default, the window sits centred; unlocked, it moves by the top edge of the card and resizes from every edge and corner, inside the screen and down to minSize.

Pass storageKey to remember the lock and the moved rect, or keep them in the app with locked, onLockChange, defaultRect and onRectChange. Locking snaps the window back to the centre; unlocking puts it back where it was moved.
UtilityScreen uses header; WorkspaceScreen and StageScreen put a ScreenPage inside the title bar window; InfoScreen keeps the title bar alone.
The container does not scroll: the children pick how they scroll, with a ScrollArea or their own layout.
Keep extra to a few small controls; the close button always comes last.
size goes to the ScreenLayer: fill by default, compact for one short task, info for a small window to read with no tools, as InfoScreen sets.
Set square for a window shown fullscreen: it drops the corner radius and the outer border.

The window is a container named screen-window. Fit content to the window with @container screen-window, never with a media query on the viewport: the window can sit in a gallery frame, a split pane or a window of its own.
Short of room, the title bar puts the subtitle on a line under the title, and extra folds away before the title shrinks.
a11y: The card is a modal dialog named by the title.
The close button carries the Close label from the strings.
Escape calls onClose once no menu, popover or dialog is open above the window, so one press closes one thing.

With titleRow={false}, the text of the corner chip names the dialog. The chip is not a control: it takes no focus, and its icon is hidden from screen readers. With cornerTitle={false}, the title still names the dialog.
With titleRow={false}, the corner X keeps the Close label and shows a tooltip with the Esc key; the lock is a toggle button with aria-pressed, named Lock window position.
Unlocked, the top edge is a Move window button after the corner buttons in the Tab order: the arrow keys move the window by 16 px, and by 64 px with Shift.

components.name: SeatCard
components.job: One seat of a lobby: who sits there with a name, a meta line and actions, an open seat, a seat that needs the user, or a dashed card that adds a seat.
useWhen: A screen shows the places of a session as a game lobby, such as the agents of a project, the players of a match or the seats of a table.
Some places are taken, some are open, and the user adds one more from the same grid.
One taken seat needs the user, such as an agent waiting for an answer, and must stand out from the rest.

avoidWhen.case: Items of a catalogue the user browses, with media, tags and details.
Many items read as one line each, in a list.
A box of content under a header row with its own actions.

rules: Set state to filled, attention, empty or add. Put the cards in a SeatGrid so they share one size and wrap.
A filled seat takes name and, optionally, lead (an avatar, an icon or any node), meta (one short line) and actions.
Pass onSelect to a filled seat when it opens something; the name becomes the one button of the card and a click anywhere on the card goes through it.
Use attention for a filled seat that waits on the user, and give reason a short phrase, such as Waiting for your answer. The colour is never the only signal.
An empty seat takes label, such as Seat 3, and a short hint, such as Invite a player. It is quiet and not clickable.
The add seat is a dashed button. Its label names what it adds, such as Add an agent, and onSelect only asks: the app adds the seat.
Give a filled seat at most one or two actions; more fold under More, danger ones asking first.
a11y: The name of a filled seat is a heading, level 3 by default, so a screen reader can jump from seat to seat.
With onSelect the name is the one button of the card, and the focus ring circles the card.
The add seat is a real button named by its label, a tab stop with a focus ring.
An attention seat says why in text with the reason, so it is heard and seen.

path: the seats of a lobby, taken, open or to add
tree.rule: SeatCard gives every lobby the same four seats, with who sits there, the open seat and the add button in fixed places.

components.name: SeatGrid
components.job: The grid that lays seat cards side by side and wraps them to the width, with the same gap and the same smallest width for every seat.
useWhen: A lobby shows its seats as cards that should fill the row and wrap to the next one on a narrow screen.
Taken, open and add seats sit in one grid and must line up at the same size.

avoidWhen.case: Cards of any kind laid out on columns or a smallest width in pixels.
A long grid of equal tiles drawn only where it is in view.

rules: Put SeatCard children in it; the columns are as many as fit at minWidth, and they share the free width.
Pick minWidth sm, md or lg for the smallest a seat gets; md is the default.
Pick gap xs, sm, md or lg for the space between seats; md is the default.
Pass label to name the grid, such as Agents of the project.
a11y: The grid is a group named by label, so the seats are heard as one set.
The order of the children is the reading and the tab order; put the add seat last.

path: the seats of a lobby, taken, open or to add
tree.rule: SeatGrid gives every lobby the same wrapping grid of seats, with the sizes set by tokens.

components.name: SectionTimeline
components.job: A vertical list of links to the sections of a long page, in titled groups, beside a line that fills as the reader scrolls.
useWhen: A long page, such as a website or a manual, has sections in groups and the reader needs to see where they are.
The list sits in a side column that stays in view while the page scrolls.

avoidWhen.case: The sections are shown as pills in the header of a page.
The list switches between the screens of a window.
The steps of one task are shown with a done state.

rules: Pass groups, each with an id, a label and children; a child has an id, a label and the href of its section.
Pass activeId for the section in view; the host owns it, as with HeaderAnchorNav.
Pass onJump to follow a link yourself, such as a smooth scroll or a route; the browser then does not jump.
Pass timeline="scroll" to fill the line from the scroll of the page, or a name such as "--page" for a view timeline you set on the sections.
Set timeline-scope with that name on a common parent of the page and the timeline, so the line can read it.
Without scroll-driven animation, or with reduced motion, the line jumps to progress, or to the active section when progress is left out.
Pass progress from 0 to 1 when you track the scroll yourself; it wins over activeId.
Pass state="idle" to dim it until the pointer or focus enters, and state="hidden" to remove it, such as on a narrow page.
a11y: It is a nav named by ariaLabel, holding a list of groups; each group is a list named by its title.
The active link has aria-current="location"; a hidden timeline is out of the reading order.
The line and its fill are decorative and hidden from screen readers.
With reduced motion the fill jumps instead of animating, and it never runs a time-based animation.

path: between sections of one long page
tree.rule: SectionTimeline is the side list of a long page: grouped section links beside a line that fills as the page scrolls.

components.name: ShortcutList
components.job: A list of keys, clicks and drags and what each one does, with the keys in one column and the descriptions in the next.
useWhen: A panel, a menu or a help screen lists the keys and gestures a tool answers to.
Some shortcuts only work at certain moments, such as while dragging, and read better under a heading of their own.

avoidWhen.case: One key or one combination sits inside a sentence, a button or a menu item.
The keys should be shown on a drawn keyboard, pressed in turn.

rules: Lead each description with what happens, in a short phrase; keep the key cell to keys or one gesture.
Write a gesture as an icon and a short verb, such as Drag title or Drag gap, never as a sentence.
Group rows by when they work, with a short heading such as Any time or While dragging, and drop words the heading already says.
Use size xs in menus, panels and cards, and md on a page of its own.
a11y: Each group is a description list: the keys are the term and the description its definition, so a screen reader reads them in pairs.
Keycaps read their full key names, and a gesture reads its label.
Pass label to name the whole list, and a group label names its group.

path: a status, a count or a label
a list of keys and what they do
tree.rule: ShortcutList keeps every key in one column and every description at one edge, however long the text runs.

components.name: SideNav
components.job: The side list of a window with several sections: a column of icons that a chevron on its edge opens to show the labels.
useWhen: A window has several top-level sections and the user moves between them from a side list.
The list needs a top block with Home and a few pages under it, then labelled groups below.

avoidWhen.case: The nav sits beside a content pane that shows the page and the search results.
A side panel with a heading folds beside the main view.
The pages are chosen from the header of a site.

rules: Pass config with groups, each with an id, an optional label and its items; an item has an id, a label and an icon.
Pass config.home for the Home row at the very top.
Pass config.top for more top-level pages under Home, in the same top block: no heading, and one divider after the whole block.
The top block is the search field, then Home, then the top pages; nothing else is drawn between them.
Leave the label of a group out for a group with no heading and no gap; prefer config.top for pages that belong under Home.
Pass activeId and onSelect; the host owns the active page.
Pass badge on an item for a count pill, which shows as a dot over the icon when the nav is collapsed.
Pass search to add a field that grows when the nav opens; the host owns the query and shows the results.
Pass defaultOpen, open with onOpenChange, or storageKey to set and keep the choice; overlay slides the open nav over the content.
Pass variant="rail" for the screen list of an app, flush on the window edge.
a11y: It is a nav named by ariaLabel, and each group is a group named by its label; a group with no label has no name.
The edge toggle says Show or Hide the navigation pane and reports aria-expanded.
The active item reports aria-current; a disabled item stays in the list but takes no click.

path: between pages, from a side list
tree.rule: SideNav is the one side list of a window: icons that open to labels, a top block with Home and pages, then labelled groups.

components.name: SidePanel
components.job: The one side panel of Tessera: a sunken panel beside the main view, with a heading, that the user drags wider or narrower and that folds to a rail.
useWhen: A screen has an outline, a layer list or an inspector beside its main view.
The user needs the room of the panel now and then, so it folds to a rail with its actions, its title and its icons.
A page has pickers on its sides, such as a list of profiles on the left and device cards to drag on the right.

avoidWhen.case: A list, an editor and an inspector make one studio screen.
A list sits beside the detail of the picked item.
The left side is the navigation of the app.

rules: Use it for every panel that folds or resizes beside a main view, other than the navigation of the app; draw no panel of your own.
Put it in a flex row beside the main view, with no bar or frame around it; it keeps its own width, and the main view takes the rest.
Pass side="end" for a panel on the right; its dashed outside border, overlapping fold button and rail mirror to its left.
Every panel resizes: there is no switch to turn it off. To hold a width, pass the same number to minWidth and maxWidth; the line still folds the panel.
Dragging the line about 32 px narrower than minWidth folds the panel to its rail, and dragging the line of a rail outward opens it; the arrow keys at the end of the range do the same.
Pass action for a button in the heading, such as Add or Rescan; the folded rail reserves its top slot and shows the button there when present.
Pass railItems as an array of item icons; the folded rail shows them under the title.
Pass containers for the expanded body. Each container has a required heading and body; use a meaningful section title distinct from the pane title.
The dashed primary border is the resize edge; it brightens and glows while hovered, focused or dragged.

The border stays on the pane while expanded and folded; the chevron straddles it at the center of the actual heading row. Folding animates the pane, heading, body and rail, with motion disabled for reduced-motion preferences.
A glow around a rail icon, such as a drop-shadow on a ready device, spreads past the rail; only a rail too long to fit scrolls and clips it.
Put every expanded section in a container with title and content. The side panel keeps the sections mounted while folded and its body scrolls with the primary slim scrollbar.
Pass width, minWidth and maxWidth in pixels; when width is outside the default 224 to 448 range the range grows to take it, so a width of 192 stays 192.
Pass storageKey to keep the width, and the fold under storageKey:collapsed.
Pass collapsed with onCollapsedChange when the app holds the fold; collapsible={false} drops the fold button.
a11y: It is an aside named by its title, with the title as a heading, h2 unless level says otherwise; showTitle={false} hides only the pane heading.
The fold button says Hide or Show and the title and reports aria-expanded; focus moves to it when the panel folds, by the button, Enter, an arrow key or a drag, and stays on it when the panel opens.
While folded the heading and the body are hidden from screen readers and the keyboard; the actions and the rail take their place, and the sideways title is hidden from screen readers.
The line is a separator: the arrow keys resize it, an arrow key at the end of the range folds or opens the panel, and Enter folds or opens it.
